meta.title: ENMAEYA Funding & Opportunities Dashboard
meta.subtitle: Lebanon development projects, funding relationships, and where they lead
meta.footnote: Illustrative prototype only. Funding amounts and relationships require final cleaning and validation.

what.title: What is this?
what.html: This dashboard tracks development funding in Lebanon — showing where money is allocated across government ministries, sectors, implementing organizations, and geographic locations. It's built to make this information accessible to the public, promoting transparency and helping users understand the country's development landscape.

why.title: Why it matters
why.html:
Development funding shapes which sectors expand, where jobs are created, and where innovation opportunities emerge.

  • Students can see which fields have growing demand
  • Job seekers can spot expanding sectors and active employers
  • Startups can find underserved sectors and procurement openings
  • NGOs and researchers can track donors, gaps, and partnership openings

mission.title: Mission & Vision
mission.html:
Mission: make development funding in Lebanon transparent, accessible, and understandable — giving the public what it needs to see national priorities, emerging sectors, and the opportunities they create for education, employment, entrepreneurship, and research.

Vision: a Lebanon where development information is open and accessible to everyone, enabling more informed decisions by citizens, institutions, businesses, and development partners.

scatter.note: Each bubble is a Lebanese ministry; bubble size indicates the breadth of its partner network. Edit projects (0-40), fundingM (0-60) and partners (0-10) — positions are calculated automatically.

all.main: Health and Development together account for over half of tracked funding, while Education and AI & Technology remain comparatively small despite their long-run relevance to Lebanon's recovery — a gap worth watching.
all.funding: Health leads overall funding at $68M, nearly six times the size of AI & Technology ($12M) — the widest spread across sectors.
all.flow: The World Bank, EU, and UNICEF each anchor a distinct sector-ministry relationship, pointing to a concentrated rather than diversified funder base across ministries.
all.location: Beirut and Mount Lebanon together host 46% of geographically-located projects, while national/unspecified projects remain the single largest category — a possible transparency gap.
all.heat: UNDP shows the broadest cross-sector presence, ranking as a top partner in four of five sectors — the closest thing to a generalist funder in this data.
all.scatter: MoPH combines high funding with high project count; MoPWT sits at the other extreme, with few projects and 57% of its funding from a single source — a concentration risk worth flagging.

students: Development, health, and social-sector fields show the most active project pipelines right now.
Programs in public health, environmental policy, and social protection align closely with current funding priorities.
jobseekers: Health and Development show the highest project volume, suggesting steadier hiring demand in those sectors.
Beirut and Mount Lebanon concentrate the most project activity, and likely the most roles.
startups: AI & Technology is the smallest funded sector — a potential underserved niche for new ventures.
66 projects are recorded nationally rather than regionally, suggesting demand for solutions that scale beyond one area.
ngos: World Bank, EU, and UNICEF are the most active funders to approach for partnership conversations.
MoSA's broad partner network (9 organizations) suggests openness to new implementing partners.
researchers: AI & Technology and Education are comparatively data-poor and underfunded relative to their long-run importance.
Funder concentration (e.g. MoPWT's 57% single-funder dependency) is a notable risk area worth investigating.

health.main: Health receives the largest share of reported funding ($68M), yet Education — critical for long-run human capital and growth — receives roughly a third of that. This imbalance may point to future opportunities in education, or to unmet needs where health investment isn't yet translating into workforce outcomes.
health.funding: At $68M, Health is Lebanon's most heavily funded sector — about 1.3x the size of Development, the next largest.
health.flow: The World Bank funds 42% of the Ministry of Public Health's tracked funding, a dependency worth monitoring against diversification efforts.
health.location: MoPH activity skews national and Beirut-based, consistent with the concentration of tertiary healthcare infrastructure in the capital.
health.heat: WHO (5) and UNICEF (4) dominate health partnerships, with World Bank and UNDP in secondary roles — a relatively concentrated partner base.
health.scatter: MoPH sits in the high-funding, high-activity quadrant, indicating a sector with both scale and sustained donor engagement.

students: Rising demand for public health, epidemiology, and health-systems management graduates.
Digital health and health informatics are emerging but still underrepresented skill areas.
jobseekers: MoPH's 38 recorded projects suggest steady hiring across public health, program management, and M&E roles.
WHO, UNICEF, and World Bank are active employers and implementing partners in this sector.
startups: Digital health and medical-supply procurement remain comparatively underserved niches.
High donor funding paired with a concentrated partner base suggests room for new implementing organizations.
ngos: WHO and UNICEF are the most active health funders/partners to approach for consortium opportunities.
MoPH's high project count signals capacity for additional implementing partnerships.
researchers: Health-financing sustainability and the 42% World Bank dependency are underexplored questions.
Little visible link yet between health investment and workforce/economic outcomes — a research gap.

education.main: Education receives just $24M — about a third of Health's funding — despite being a core driver of long-run productivity and youth employment. The gap suggests education may be an underfunded priority relative to its economic importance.
education.funding: Education ranks fourth of five sectors at $24M, ahead only of AI & Technology.
education.flow: UNICEF funds 39% of the Ministry of Education's tracked funding — the lowest top-funder concentration among the four flows shown, implying a slightly more diversified funder base.
education.location: Education projects are not separately mapped here, but sit within the broader national and Beirut-weighted pattern seen across sectors.
education.heat: UNICEF (5) is the dominant education partner; World Bank (3) and ILO (2) play secondary roles, with UNDP and FAO largely absent.
education.scatter: MoEHE sits mid-chart on both axes — moderate funding, moderate activity — neither a clear priority nor clearly neglected.

students: Education data gaps mean there's real room to specialize in education economics, learning assessment, or ed-tech.
Youth-unemployment-linked fields (skills training, vocational education) look increasingly relevant.
jobseekers: Fewer recorded education projects than health or development suggest a smaller, more competitive job pool for now.
UNICEF and World Bank are the main organizations active in this space.
startups: Ed-tech and skills-training platforms remain a comparatively open field given low sector funding.
Underfunding relative to need may translate into procurement or grant openings as donor attention shifts.
ngos: UNICEF is the anchor funder-partner; ILO's presence points to a training/livelihoods angle worth pairing with education work.
Lower overall funding may mean less competition for new partnerships here than in Health.
researchers: Education data gaps in Arab LDCs remain a known, underexplored area — directly relevant to Enmaeya's own prior coverage.
The link between education funding and youth unemployment outcomes is a live research question.

economy.main: Economy sector data is not yet available in this dataset — check back once funding figures for this sector have been collected and validated.

environment.main: Environment funding ($32M) sits mid-pack, but its funder base is the most concentrated of the four flows shown — 51% from the EU alone — meaning sector momentum may be closely tied to a single donor's priorities.
environment.funding: Environment ranks third at $32M, roughly 47% of Health's total.
environment.flow: The EU funds 51% of the Ministry of Energy and Water's tracked funding — the highest single-funder share among the four flows shown.
environment.location: Environmental projects follow the same national/Beirut-weighted pattern seen elsewhere, without a distinct regional cluster in this data.
environment.heat: FAO (5) and UNDP (5) co-lead environment partnerships, giving the sector two strong anchor partners rather than one.
environment.scatter: MoEW and MoA cluster in the lower-funding, lower-activity region — smaller in scale than Health or Development, but not without partner depth.

students: Environmental policy, water resource management, and climate-adaptation fields align with FAO/UNDP-led programming.
Agricultural economics is increasingly relevant given FAO's strong presence.
jobseekers: FAO and UNDP are the sector's main active employers/partners to track.
Lower project counts than Health mean fewer but more specialized roles.
startups: EU's 51% funding share signals a sector with real momentum, but limited beyond that single donor — worth watching donor diversification.
Water and energy-efficiency solutions look aligned with current ministry-level funding.
ngos: FAO and UNDP are the strongest potential consortium partners in this sector.
High single-funder dependency (EU) may mean openings if the EU diversifies its implementing partners.
researchers: Donor concentration risk (51% from one funder) is a clear, quantifiable research question.
Climate and environment financing in Lebanon remains a comparatively thin evidence base.

ai.main: AI & Technology is by far the smallest funded sector ($12M, 18% of Health's total), despite Lebanon's active push toward digital transformation — this gap between policy ambition and funding may be the clearest opportunity signal in the dataset.
ai.funding: AI & Technology is the smallest tracked sector at $12M — less than a fifth of Health's funding.
ai.flow: No dedicated funder→ministry flow is shown for AI & Technology in this dataset yet, itself a data gap worth flagging.
ai.location: AI & Technology projects aren't separately geo-mapped here; most likely cluster in Beirut given the sector's institutional base.
ai.heat: UNDP (4) is the only partner with a meaningful presence in AI & Technology — every other tracked organization shows little to no activity.
ai.scatter: MoET sits at the lower end of both funding and project count — a sector still early in attracting large-scale, multi-partner investment.

students: AI, data science, and digital-governance skills are in growing demand relative to current (thin) supply of funded programs.
This is the sector with the widest gap between ambition (MITAI's mandate) and funding — worth watching closely.
jobseekers: Fewer recorded projects mean a smaller current job pool, but a first-mover advantage as funding likely grows.
UNDP is currently the most visible partner organization in this space.
startups: The clearest underserved sector in the entire dataset — low funding, few partners, but strong policy attention.
Digital-government and AI-readiness procurement may open up as MITAI's mandate translates into funded projects.
ngos: Very few funders are currently active here — an open field for organizations positioning early in AI & Technology.
Partnering with UNDP, the sector's lone visible anchor, may be the fastest entry point.
researchers: The funding-ambition gap in AI & Technology is a clear, underexplored research question.
Almost no partner-network data exists for this sector — a genuine data gap to document.

development.main: Development is the second-largest funded sector ($54M) and has the broadest implementing-partner network (MoSA: 9 organizations) — suggesting a sector that's both well-resourced and structurally open to new partnerships.
development.funding: Development ranks second at $54M, about 79% of Health's total.
development.flow: The EU funds 48% of the Ministry of Social Affairs' tracked funding, the second-highest single-funder concentration among the four flows shown.
development.location: Development projects likely track closely with the national/unspecified category (66 projects), consistent with cross-regional social-protection programming.
development.heat: UNICEF (5) and UNDP (5) co-lead development partnerships, with FAO (4) and ILO (4) also strongly present — the most multi-partner sector in the heatmap.
development.scatter: MoSA sits in the high-funding, high-activity quadrant alongside MoPH, with the largest bubble size (9 partners) — the sector with the widest partner network.

students: Social protection, livelihoods, and community development fields align with MoSA's broad partner base.
Multi-stakeholder program design is a valuable skill given the sector's dense partner network.
jobseekers: MoSA's 9-partner network suggests the widest range of potential employers of any ministry tracked.
UNICEF, UNDP, FAO, and ILO are all actively engaged — more entry points than most sectors.
startups: A well-resourced sector, but with 9 partners already active, differentiation matters more than sector access.
Livelihoods and social-enterprise models may find natural entry points via existing implementing partners.
ngos: MoSA's openness (9 partners) makes it one of the more accessible ministries for new consortium relationships.
EU (48% share) and UNICEF/UNDP are the funders most worth approaching.
researchers: The EU's 48% concentration despite a 9-partner network is a notable tension worth investigating.
Development sits second in funding but its outcomes data is less visible than Health's — a reporting gap.

ministryProjects.project: IPC Acute Food Insecurity Analysis for Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: The IPC analysis on Lebanon was developed by FAO, WFP and the Ministry of Agriculture, showing 1.65 million people in crisis or emergency levels of food insecurity, up from 1.26 million before the escalation.

ministryProjects.project: IPC acute food insecurity analysis following the 2024 conflict
ministryProjects.description: An IPC analysis developed by FAO, WFP and the Ministry of Agriculture found 1.65 million people in Lebanon facing crisis or emergency food insecurity (IPC Phase 3 or above), up from 1.26 million before the escalation, with 201,000 at emergency levels.

ministryProjects.project: Sustainable Fisheries Resources Management and Climate Resilience in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and FAO held a technical workshop on environmentally sound management of marine litter and discarded fishing nets under the Norway-funded fisheries and climate resilience project, jointly implemented by the Ministry and FAO.

ministryProjects.project: Emergency and Livelihood Support in the Agrifood Sector, Conflict-Affected Areas
ministryProjects.description: Italy approved a EUR 5 million contribution to FAO for emergency agricultural and livelihood assistance in conflict-affected areas, implemented in close coordination with the Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and targeting at least 9,850 households.

ministryProjects.project: Contributing to Food Security for Refugees and Host Communities Living in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, the EU, FAO and WFP are advancing this EU-funded project, which strengthens farmers' productive capacity through cash-based support, technical training, land rehabilitation grants and irrigation infrastructure such as hill lakes.

ministryProjects.project: Virtual training programme for farmers on apple and vegetable value chains
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and FAO, funded by Canada, launched a comprehensive online training programme for over 2,200 farmers (883 women, 1,323 men) on good agricultural practices, crop management and season planning.

ministryProjects.project: Recovery and Resilience of Agrifood Systems and Rural Livelihoods, South Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and FAO launched a Japan-funded project supporting agriculture-based livelihoods for about 230 vulnerable farming households (1,150 individuals) in the South and Nabatiyeh governorates, with at least 30 per cent women beneficiaries.

ministryProjects.project: Emergency support to control the Foot and Mouth Disease outbreak
ministryProjects.description: FAO and the Minister of Agriculture signed a project providing emergency support to control the Foot and Mouth Disease outbreak, prioritising the second phase of the emergency vaccination campaign and disease surveillance procedures.

ministryProjects.project: Strengthening Resilience of Vulnerable Smallholder Farm Families
ministryProjects.description: FAO, the Ministry of Agriculture and Canada held the closing and sustainability workshop of the five-year project launched in 2021 to enhance livelihoods and food security for vulnerable smallholder farmers.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon's Pandemic Fund: One Health Approach to Drive Resilience and Recovery
ministryProjects.description: Under this three-year project funded by The Pandemic Fund, the Ministry of Agriculture and FAO held a four-day training on epidemiology and disease surveillance for 45 veterinarians and animal health staff.

ministryProjects.project: Strengthening Institutional Governance of the Ministry of Agriculture
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Agriculture and the FAO Representative signed a two-year project to enhance the Ministry's institutional framework and capacity to manage and implement agricultural policies, programmes and services.

ministryProjects.project: Safe disposal of obsolete pesticide stocks
ministryProjects.description: Following a formal request from the Ministry of Agriculture, FAO will support the safe disposal of obsolete pesticide stocks, under a second agreement signed by the Minister and the FAO Representative.

ministryProjects.project: Agricultural Livelihoods and Employment through Land Reclamation and Water Reservoirs
ministryProjects.description: Under this FAO project funded by the Netherlands, twenty Green Plan staff (11 men, 9 women) were trained on orchard establishment, variety and rootstock selection and investment costs. Green Plan is affiliated to the Ministry of Agriculture.

ministryProjects.project: Enhancing the Resilience of Vulnerable Refugee Communities through Cash-for-Work
funders: Ministry of Foreign Affairs of the Republic of Korea
ministryProjects.description: Korea and FAO signed an MoU for a cash-for-work reforestation project in Anjar with a USD 500,000 contribution, implemented with AFDC and LRI in collaboration with the Ministry of Agriculture and the Municipality of Anjar.

ministryProjects.project: SALMA project - 2019 reforestation and afforestation campaign
ministryProjects.description: The GEF-funded, FAO-led SALMA project began its 2019 reforestation and afforestation campaign with the Ministry of Agriculture, municipalities and NGOs, planting around 9,000 seedlings, in support of the Ministry's 40 Million Trees Programme.

ministryProjects.project: Upgrading the Technical Agriculture Education System in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: This FAO-led project funded by the Netherlands and implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Agriculture, UNICEF, ILO and AVSI enhances the employability of young Lebanese and displaced Syrians through technical agriculture education.

ministryProjects.project: Towards the Enhancement of the Mediterranean Diet: The Case of Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: FAO, the Ministry of Agriculture and AUB's Faculty of Agriculture and Food Science held an inception workshop launching this Italy-funded regional project on dietary consumption patterns and healthy diet policies.

ministryProjects.project: National Center for Forest Seeds of Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: FAO and the Ministry of Agriculture launched the 'National Center for Forest Seeds of Lebanon' project at an inception workshop; it is funded by Norway with an estimated budget of USD 373,032 over two years, in partnership with LARI.

ministryProjects.project: Smart Adaptation of Forest Landscapes in Mountain Areas (SALMA)
ministryProjects.description: FAO and the Ministry of Agriculture announced the signing of the five-year SALMA project, funded by GEF with a budget of USD 7,147,635, to be implemented from December 2016 with the Ministries of Agriculture and Environment.

ministryProjects.project: FAO Lebanon Country Programming Framework 2016-2019
ministryProjects.description: FAO launched its Lebanon Country Programming Framework 2016-2019 at the Grand Serail under the patronage of the Prime Minister; the document was signed by FAO and the Ministry of Agriculture to strengthen cooperation on agriculture, food security and natural resources.

ministryProjects.project: EIIP support to Green Plan's Greening the Lands project in North Lebanon
funders: German Government through KfW Development Bank
ministryProjects.description: The ILO's Employment-Intensive Infrastructure Programme, funded by Germany through KfW, supports the Green Plan under the Ministry of Agriculture's Greening the Lands project. A joint field visit reviewed land reclamation and water conservation works in North Lebanon.

ministryProjects.project: Land reclamation and water reservoirs matching grants (Green Plan)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, through its Green Plan, launched a demand-driven matching grants programme for more than 1,000 small-scale farmers to reclaim land and build water reservoirs, funded by Denmark and implemented by FAO; over 100 farmers have signed agreements.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Agricultural Damage and Loss Assessment (DIEM-Impact)
ministryProjects.description: FAO, with the Ministry of Agriculture and CNRS-L, launched a damage and loss assessment for October 2023-November 2024 estimating USD 118 million in damages and USD 586 million in losses, and sector recovery needs of USD 263 million.

ministryProjects.project: Crop certification programme for Lebanese agricultural exports to the EU
partners: Industry and Agriculture of Zahle and the Bekaa
ministryProjects.description: The ILO, CCIAZ and the Ministry of Agriculture launched a partnership at a signing ceremony in Zahle to develop a certification programme helping agricultural exporters meet EU standards, starting with cherries then prunes and citrus, under the Sida-funded BOUZOUR project.

ministryProjects.project: EIIP Lebanon / Greening the Lands programme achievements
funders: German Government through KfW Development Bank
ministryProjects.description: Lebanon's Greening the Lands programme, run by the ILO EIIP with the Ministry of Agriculture's Green Plan and LRI and funded by Germany through KfW, has created over 1 million worker days, rehabilitated over 1,000 farms and built 817 water reservoirs.

ministryProjects.project: BOUZOUR - awareness sessions on EU export compliance for cherry producers
partners: Industry and Agriculture of Zahle and the Bekaa
ministryProjects.description: Through the Sida-funded BOUZOUR project, the ILO supported two awareness sessions organized by CCIAZ and the Ministry of Agriculture in Zahle and Hammana, where the Ministry presented updated EU compliance guidelines to cherry farmers and agricultural SMEs.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon IPC acute food insecurity analysis, April-October 2025
ministryProjects.description: The Lebanon Integrated Food Security Phase Classification report for April-October 2025 was launched at the Ministry of Agriculture headquarters in Beirut under the patronage of Minister Nizar Hani, with WFP and FAO participation.

ministryProjects.project: IPC food security analysis April-October 2025
ministryProjects.description: The Lebanon IPC report for April-October 2025 was launched at the Ministry of Agriculture headquarters under the patronage of Minister Nizar Hani, with WFP and FAO; it found around 1.17 million people facing crisis or emergency acute food insecurity.

ministryProjects.project: Greening the Lands under EIIP - agricultural water reservoirs
funders: German Government through KfW Development Bank
ministryProjects.description: A field visit showcased the ILO's Greening the Lands initiative with the Ministry of Agriculture, under the Employment-Intensive Infrastructure Programme funded by Germany via KfW and the Netherlands-funded PROSPECTS Partnership.

ministryProjects.project: Greening the Lands - agricultural land reclamation under ENABLE
ministryProjects.description: Under the EU-funded ENABLE programme, the ILO works with the Ministry of Agriculture through the Green Plan and LRI to reclaim agricultural land, build water reservoirs and retaining walls, aiming to reach 43 farms in 20 villages in Southern Nabatieh.

ministryProjects.project: BOUZOUR Project - Responsible Business Conduct training for agri-food sector
ministryProjects.description: The ILO concluded a three-day training on Responsible Business Conduct and export readiness for the agri-food sector under the Sweden-funded BOUZOUR Project. Participants included representatives of the Ministries of Agriculture, Economy and Trade and Industry.

ministryProjects.project: Souk El Jabal agricultural, environmental and eco-tourism complex
funders: Government of Germany through KfW Development Bank
partners: Union of Chouf El Sweijani Municipalities
ministryProjects.description: Souk El Jabal, established by UNDP with the Union of Chouf El Sweijani Municipalities and German funding through KfW, was inaugurated in Upper Chouf in the presence of the Minister of Agriculture. It will benefit over 270 farmers, 400 beekeepers and 40 agro-food producers.

ministryProjects.project: BOUZOUR project - cherry export certification and pest control
partners: Industry and Agriculture of Zahle and Bekaa
ministryProjects.description: Under the Sweden-funded ILO BOUZOUR project, the Ministry of Agriculture and CCIAZ are helping cherry farmers adopt better pest-control methods and are establishing an export certification programme for cherries and stone fruits meeting EU standards.

ministryProjects.project: Training on the role of cooperatives in eliminating child labour
ministryProjects.description: The ILO and the General Directorate of Cooperatives at the Ministry of Agriculture concluded a two-day training (20-21 November 2025) building the capacity of cooperative leaders to identify, prevent and respond to child labour.

ministryProjects.project: Enhancing Recovery and Resilience of Agrifood Systems in South Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and FAO launched a Japan-funded project supporting agriculture-based livelihoods for about 230 vulnerable farming households (1,150 individuals) in crop and livestock production across South and Nabatiyeh, at least 30 percent women.

ministryProjects.project: FAO Lebanon Emergency and Resilience Plan (ERP) 2026-2028
ministryProjects.description: FAO's Emergency and Resilience Plan 2026-2028 combines emergency assistance and resilience building for farmers and rural communities, with a total budget of USD 65,770,000 aiming to reach 48,855 households, implemented with national and international partners.

ministryProjects.project: IPC acute food insecurity analysis April-August 2026
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture, with FAO and WFP, released an IPC projected analysis showing 1.24 million people are expected to face Crisis (IPC Phase 3) or worse food insecurity between April and August 2026, up from 874,000 in the previous period.

ministryProjects.project: Production of 1.5 million vegetable seedlings (Together for Food Security)
funders: German Government through KfW Development Bank
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Agriculture and UNDP launched a project to produce and distribute 1.5 million vegetable seedlings, funded by Germany through KfW Development Bank, under the Together for Food Security campaign. First phase covers 500,000 seedlings.

ministryProjects.project: Comprehensive assessment of agricultural damage and losses in South Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: A joint assessment by CNRS-L and the Ministry of Agriculture, with technical support from UNDP, FAO and WFP, found USD 41.2 million in direct agricultural damage over 1,380 hectares and USD 530.5 million in production losses across 56,320 hectares.

ministryProjects.project: Agricultural drones project funded by China
partners: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of China
ministryProjects.description: Agriculture Minister Nizar Hani and the Chinese ambassador reviewed executive steps of joint projects, notably the Chinese-funded agricultural drones project supporting pest control and monitoring of natural resources.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon-China agricultural cooperation agreement
partners: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs of the People's Republic of China
ministryProjects.description: The two sides assessed progress on finalising an agricultural cooperation agreement between the Lebanese Ministry of Agriculture and China's Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs, covering research, capacity building and technology transfer.

ministryProjects.project: AHEAD programme: livestock and feed support for farmers in Jezzine
ministryProjects.description: Malta Lebanon, with the Ministry of Agriculture and under Minister Nizar Hani's patronage, launched an initiative distributing feed and agricultural inputs to livestock breeders in Jezzine under the AHEAD programme, funded by the German Federal Foreign Office.

ministryProjects.project: Renovation of Mar Mikhael train station into a cultural space
ministryProjects.description: UNESCO's Director-General laid the foundation stone for the renovation of the Mar Mikhael train station, a 10,000 sqm ruin to be transformed by UNESCO and UN-Habitat into a cultural and living space, with USD 3.5 million funding by Italy; opening in 2027.

ministryProjects.project: Restoration of the Grand Theatre of Beirut (first phase)
ministryProjects.description: The Grand Theatre, closed since 1990 and damaged in 2020, will undergo restoration. First-phase funding of USD 1 million by the United Arab Emirates will stabilize the building and develop a cultural project with the municipality and the Ministry of Culture.

ministryProjects.project: LiBeirut initiative for urban, cultural and school rehabilitation
ministryProjects.description: The LiBeirut initiative launched after the port explosions has mobilized more than USD 45 million for the capital's reconstruction, coordinating rehabilitation of 280 educational establishments, equipping 126 public schools and training over 1,000 teachers.

ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation of Mar Mikhael Train Station "Industrial Heritage Park"
funders: Government of Italy through the Italian Agency for Development Cooperation
ministryProjects.description: The Rehabilitation of the Mar Mikhael Train Station Industrial Heritage Park project, initiated by the Railway and Public Transport Authority and the Directorate General of Antiquities, is funded by Italy through AICS and implemented by UNESCO. Conservation work is ongoing.

ministryProjects.project: National Network for the Protection of Libraries, Archives and Cultural Heritage
ministryProjects.description: Culture Minister Ghassan Salame patronised the launch of the National Network for the Protection of Libraries, Archives and Cultural Heritage at the National Library in Sanayeh, alongside a global Beirut Appeal and damage documentation database.

ministryProjects.project: Million Book Campaign to rebuild damaged libraries
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Culture announced a forthcoming 'million book' campaign to help rebuild private, semi-public and public libraries, in cooperation with Amel Foundation, the Cultural Movement Antelias and the National Library of Baaqline.

ministryProjects.project: Start and Improve Your Business (SIYB) Training of Trainers
ministryProjects.description: The ILO launched a Start and Improve Your Business Training of Trainers workshop in Beirut (4-15 April) in partnership with the Ministry of Economy and Trade, the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Lebanese University, under projects funded by the EU, the Netherlands and Sweden.

ministryProjects.project: Workshop on accessing the Saudi market for Lebanese exporters
partners: Chambers of Commerce Industry and Agriculture
ministryProjects.description: The National Trade Assistance Office and the Ministry of Economy and Trade, with UNDP and the Government of Canada and Lebanese chambers, held a workshop on requirements, procedures and opportunities for Lebanese exporters in the Saudi market.

ministryProjects.project: Reconstruction and emergency assistance for war-damaged Nabatieh
ministryProjects.description: Economy Minister Amer Bisat toured Nabatieh and said the government is seriously seeking external assistance and speeding up repairs, referring to aid earmarked for Lebanon being redirected into emergency assistance worth USD 600 million.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: National Digital Learning Strategy for Lebanon
funders: Education Cannot Wait  through the Multi-Year Resilience Programme
ministryProjects.description: A National Digital Learning Strategy is being designed in partnership with MEHE, UNESCO and CRDP with financial support from the Multi-Year Resilience Programme funded by Education Cannot Wait, following a review of blended learning presented at a high-level roundtable.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Transition and Resilience Education Fund (TREF)
ministryProjects.description: Since the establishment of TREF, UNICEF with international partners has allocated over USD 85 million annually to MEHE education programmes, disbursing funds to 1,074 public schools, paying 14,000 special contract teachers and printing 2.8 million textbooks.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Russian scholarships and reactivation of educational cooperation agreements
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami received the Russian ambassador; talks covered Russian study scholarships for Lebanese students and agreement to reactivate and update bilateral educational cooperation agreements.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Pakistan educational cooperation agreement and student scholarships
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The Minister received the Pakistani ambassador and discussed follow-up on the educational and university cooperation agreement, notably scholarships offered to Lebanese students, and extending the agreement's application period.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Support for the education of non-Lebanese students (Education for All)
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami met UNHCR representatives to follow up on education for all and securing support for the schooling of non-Lebanese students.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Social assistance and temporary compensation decree for education staff
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: A decree published in the Official Gazette grants social assistance and temporary monthly compensation to staff of the Ministry of Education, including 13 salaries plus an attendance allowance for public school and technical institute staff, effective 1 February 2025.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Public-private school networking and IB programme with Hariri Foundation
partners: Hariri Foundation for Sustainable Human Development
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami and Bahia Hariri discussed replicating the Saida school network experience across regions and continuing the International Baccalaureate programme so public schools benefit from international standards and teacher training.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Lebanon's engagement in the Global Partnership for Education (GPE)
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Lebanon took part in the GPE conference in Vietnam through the MEHE partnerships coordinator, with support from the UNESCO Beirut office as official coordinating agency for the GPE file, and called on donors to prioritise Lebanon under GPE support frameworks.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: International Baccalaureate cooperation agreement with MEHE
partners: Hariri Foundation for Sustainable Human Development
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami met Bahia Hariri and the ministry team coordinating IB training to review steps achieved under the cooperation agreement between the Ministry and the International Baccalaureate organisation, and the next steps.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: UAE support for the Lebanese education sector
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The Minister met a high-level UAE delegation including the director of development and international cooperation at the UAE Foreign Ministry and executive director of operations at the UAE international aid agency, to discuss support for the education sector.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: AFD financing for Ministry of Education priorities
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The article reports that Minister Karami followed up with the French Development Agency on securing financing for the Ministry's priorities.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Arab Reading Challenge (9th season) in Lebanon
funders: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives
partners: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami patronised the closing ceremony of the 9th Arab Reading Challenge, organised by the Ministry's Cultural Affairs and Fine Arts Department in cooperation with Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Initiatives.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Global Partnership for Education (GPE) initiative technical working team
partners: Center for Educational Research and Development
Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Rima Karami chaired a meeting with UNICEF, UNESCO, AFD, the EU and Lebanese education bodies under the Global Partnership for Education initiative, launching a specialised technical working team.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: International Baccalaureate programme in public schools
partners: Hariri Foundation for Sustainable Human Development
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The Minister met Bahia Hariri, head of the Hariri Foundation for Sustainable Human Development, and the International Baccalaureate team to review progress with the public schools covered by the project on curriculum and teacher training.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation and equipping of crisis-affected public schools
ministryProjects.description: With JICA funding, UNOPS is supporting the Ministry of Education and Higher Education to rehabilitate and equip public schools damaged by the crisis and to provide capacity-building training to school representatives under the Ministry's School Improvement Plan.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: JICA project to strengthen school leadership and school improvement plans
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: MEHE and JICA launched a new project, implemented by UNOPS, to strengthen Lebanese school principals' leadership and management capacities and develop School Improvement Plans. It runs from July 2025 to March 2026 with a total grant of about USD 1.2 million.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Lebanon national school meals programme under the School Health Program
ministryProjects.description: Lebanon's school meals initiative, launched in 2016 with WFP support and implemented under MEHE's national School Health Program, has grown to over 107,000 children in 323 public schools; the upcoming school year is backed by six donor countries.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Local Education Group (LEG) - resource mobilization for education quality
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami chaired the third periodic Local Education Group meeting with UN agencies, embassies, donors and international agencies, reviewing the project Lebanon is developing with the group to provide resources for education and raise teaching quality.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: ENABLE Programme - healthcare assistant work-based training
partners: Directorate General of Vocational and Technical Education
ministryProjects.description: Under the EU-funded ENABLE Programme implemented by the ILO with the Safadi Foundation, DGTVET and Hospital Abou Jaoudeh, 30 young women and men qualified as healthcare assistants. A graduation ceremony was held at Hospital Abou Jaoudeh.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Mental Health and Psychosocial Support (MHPSS) Program in Lebanon
partners: Center for Educational Research and Development
ministryProjects.description: UNESCO, in partnership with MEHE and the Embassy of Japan, launched the MHPSS Program at CERD in Jounieh. The initiative will reach 10,000 students across 50 public schools with tailored psychosocial support.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: School Improvement Plan (SIP) programme - Japanese grant disbursement training
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Education and JICA concluded awareness lectures on the mechanism for disbursing the grant provided to public schools in Beirut and Mount Lebanon under the School Improvement Plan (SIP) programme, run in partnership with JICA since 2017 and implemented by UNOPS.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: National Policy on Inclusive Education for Children with Special Needs (2023)
ministryProjects.description: Development and endorsement of the MEHE 2023 National Policy on Inclusive Education for Children with Special Needs, with UNICEF technical support and EU funding, establishing a national framework to scale up inclusive education.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: MEHE Inclusive Education Programme scale-up
ministryProjects.description: The MEHE Inclusive Education Programme, supported by the EU and UNICEF since its 2018-2019 pilot, is being implemented in 117 public schools to ensure equitable access to quality education.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: MoU with the American University of Beirut on education reform and e-learning
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami and AUB President Fadlo Khuri signed a memorandum of understanding to establish a strategic partnership advancing education reform, institutional capacity, and the quality and governance of e-learning and digital learning in Lebanon.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: UNICEF support for ministry restructuring, digitization and affected schools
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami met the UNICEF Representative in Lebanon to review progress on joint projects and requested funding and support for the ministry's restructuring and computerization, and additional resources for schools in conflict-affected and severely under-resourced areas.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: EU funding plan for Lebanon's education sector 2026-2027
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami met an EU delegation led by Alessandra Viezzer to review the ministry's plan and displaced students' education. The mission briefed her on EU funding available for 2026 and 2027, noting it will decline thereafter, and offered technical support.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Provision of computers and modern teaching equipment to public schools
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: UNICEF handed over modern equipment, notably computers, to a number of public schools and secondary schools across Lebanese regions. The Ministry of Education surveyed school needs and secured the necessary funding from UNICEF before the handover.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: National school feeding programme with WFP
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami met the WFP Country Director to review implementation of the school feeding programme, which currently covers about 116,000 students through school kitchens and local food purchases, with a plan to expand to around 130,000 learners.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Education Trust Fund (TREF) donor support
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami discussed support for the trust fund (TREF) with donor bodies, alongside follow-up on school feeding and Lebanese University faculty full-time appointments.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP) - World Bank loan
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Karami met CDR and World Bank representatives to follow up the USD 250 million World Bank loan approved by Parliament in late 2025 to finance the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP), rebuilding infrastructure damaged in South Lebanon and restoring vital services.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Cooperation protocol on digital transformation, services and data protection
partners: Ministry of State for Technology and Artificial Intelligence Affairs
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Education and Higher Education and the Ministry of State for Technology and AI Affairs signed a cooperation protocol in Beirut Digital City to modernize the education ministry's digital systems, platforms and services and protect data.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: MHPSS Phase 2: Mental Health and Wellbeing of Children in Crisis-Affected Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: UNESCO and the Government of Japan signed a new cooperation agreement launching the second phase of the MHPSS Programme, working closely with MEHE to support the mental health and psychosocial wellbeing of crisis-affected students and teachers.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: National school meals programme supported by the Republic of Korea
funders: Government of the Republic of Korea
ministryProjects.description: WFP supports 325 public primary schools nationwide under the national school meals programme implemented in partnership with the Ministry of Education and Higher Education, with continued support from the Republic of Korea; the programme has reached 116,000 children.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: National school meals programme - Republic of Korea rice contribution
ministryProjects.amountRaw: 864 metric tons of rice - equivalent to over USD 1 million
ministryProjects.description: The Republic of Korea contributed 864 metric tons of rice, equivalent to over USD 1 million, to WFP Lebanon in November 2025, supporting the national school meals programme run with MEHE in 325 public primary schools and in-kind food assistance in the South.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Local Education Group (LEG) - education recovery programme
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Minister Rima Karami chaired the fifth meeting of the Local Education Group, which discussed its terms of reference and the education recovery programme involving multiple partners, and began mapping the resources needed for projects and programmes.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Teaching Hubs for education continuity for displaced populations
partners: Center for Educational Research and Development
ministryProjects.description: UNESCO allocated USD 650,000 to support education continuity for displaced populations, including renewed support from France (EUR 200,000) and Portugal (EUR 150,000) plus over USD 250,000 reallocated from Oman and Japan funding, working with MEHE to establish Teaching Hubs.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: G12++ school-leaver qualification for refugees and displaced youth
ministryProjects.description: Cambridge University Press & Assessment and NGO Alsama Project signed an agreement at the Education World Forum to develop and scale the G12++ qualification for displaced youth, signed in the presence of the Lebanese Ministry of Education & Higher Education, UK FCDO and UNESCO.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.project: Social Cohesion: The State and Shared Responsibility forum
partners: Educational Center for Research and Development
ministryProjects.description: The ministries of Education, Youth and Sports, Information and Culture jointly organised a forum on social cohesion at the National Library in Sanayeh to promote dialogue on citizenship, participation and shared responsibility.

ministryProjects.project: Bqaatet Kanaan and Chabrouh dams technical and financial review
ministryProjects.description: Minister Saddi toured the Bqaatet Kanaan and Chabrouh dams; MP Chawki Dekkache said 75 percent of the total cost of the Bqaatet Kanaan dam had been paid since 2016 while works remain unfinished, and MPs called for completing the project technically and financially.

ministryProjects.project: Power purchase agreements for three solar farms with CMA CGM (45 MW)
ministryProjects.description: Minister Saddi signed power purchase agreements (PPA) with CMA CGM's regional head Joe Dakkak after Merit Invest, part of CMA CGM, obtained three licences to build solar farms; the project is to provide 45 MW.

ministryProjects.project: Activation of the USD 250 million World Bank loan for the electricity sector
partners: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
ministryProjects.description: Minister Saddi held working meetings with World Bank and EBRD delegations, presenting sector reform plans and discussing implementation of the conditions for activating the USD 250 million loan.

ministryProjects.project: Qaraoun (Qalaa) lake pollution treatment and wastewater plants in the Bekaa
ministryProjects.description: Minister Saddi said the Ministry has been working for about a month on the lake pollution file with the Council for Development and Reconstruction, hoping treatment plants start operating soon; the file was discussed with the Italian ambassador, the central bank and donors.

ministryProjects.project: Block 8 offshore exploration and production agreement
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry referenced the signing ceremony held at the Grand Serail under the patronage of PM Nawaf Salam between Lebanon and the TotalEnergies, QatarEnergy and Eni consortium on the Block 8 gas exploration agreement.

ministryProjects.project: Award of Block 8 petroleum rights to the TotalEnergies-QatarEnergy-Eni consortium
ministryProjects.description: The Council of Ministers approved awarding Block 8 to the TotalEnergies, QatarEnergy and Eni consortium under an exploration and production agreement; the consortium committed to a 3D seismic survey over 1,200 km2 during the first exploration period.

ministryProjects.project: Zero-fee petroleum storage agreement for Lebanese industrialists
ministryProjects.description: Minister Saddi signed an agreement with the Association of Lebanese Industrialists allowing it to store LIBNOR-compliant petroleum products in tanks of the Tripoli and Zahrani oil installations at zero storage fees, for materials used exclusively in industry.

ministryProjects.project: Technical assessment of the unfinished Bqaata and Balaa dams
ministryProjects.description: The EU delegation and AFD informed Minister Saddi of approval to support an assessment of the Bqaata and Balaa dams, covering current works, additional studies, operational potential and financing required; experts are to be selected via international tender.

ministryProjects.project: Fuel shipment purchase for the army and public sector (tanker BASILIS L)
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 51 million (initially estimated at USD 24 million)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry stated the 30,000 metric tonne shipment was purchased for the military institution and the public sector as the second batch of a public tender launched on 15/12/2025; the price rose from about USD 24 million to about USD 51 million.

ministryProjects.project: Solar power system for Ain Jdideh village water well
ministryProjects.description: During a tour of Aley district Minister Saddi inaugurated the solar energy project for the Ain Jdideh village water well, after a speech by Rima Khoury of the NCA association which funded the project.

ministryProjects.project: World Bank loan to strengthen Electricite du Liban
ministryProjects.description: Parliament approved a USD 250 million World Bank loan to strengthen EDL's operational capabilities, including a national control centre, advanced metering infrastructure and rehabilitation of the Achrafieh substation damaged in the 2020 Beirut port explosion.

ministryProjects.project: 150 MW solar plant in the Bekaa
ministryProjects.description: Within the USD 250 million World Bank loan, USD 90 million is allocated for a 150 MW solar plant in the Bekaa.

ministryProjects.project: Concessional financing for the transmission and distribution grid
ministryProjects.description: Minister Saddi revealed that talks are ongoing with an Arab fund to secure financing on favourable terms for the transmission and distribution grid, warning that increasing production without fixing the grid would be pointless.

ministryProjects.project: Derisking Renewable Energy Investment (DREI) study
ministryProjects.description: The DREI study, funded by the European Union with support from the Netherlands Enterprise Agency and implemented by UNDP in coordination with the Ministry of Energy and Water, was released as a blueprint to scale up private investment in renewable energy.

ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation of El Bared Hydroelectric Plant
funders: German Federal Ministry of Economic Cooperation and Development through KfW Development Bank
ministryProjects.description: Rehabilitation works were launched at the El Bared 1 (13.5 MW) and El Bared 2 (3.7 MW) hydropower plants for the benefit of the Ministry of Energy and Water and EDL, funded by Germany via KfW with UNDP technical support. Output is expected to rise 15 per cent.

ministryProjects.project: European Investment Bank support for the wastewater sector
ministryProjects.description: Minister Joe Saddi received Ulrich Brunhuber, head of Middle East and North Africa operations at the European Investment Bank, and his delegation; talks covered Lebanon's wastewater sector and ways of providing assistance.

ministryProjects.project: Wadi Hantouch waterway cleaning and river encroachment removal in Jounieh
partners: Beirut and Mount Lebanon Water Establishment
ministryProjects.description: Jounieh's mayor said the municipality, in cooperation with the Ministry of Energy and Water, cleaned and rehabilitated the waterways in Wadi Hantouch, so no flooding occurred this year despite heavy rainfall; work continues on river encroachments.

ministryProjects.project: Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Water Award (5th cycle)
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 1 million (headline states half a million dollars)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry announced the fifth cycle of the Mohammed bin Rashid Al Maktoum Global Water Award, supervised by the UAE's Suqia foundation, open to companies, universities and individuals developing renewable-energy technologies for clean drinking water; deadline 30 April 2026.

ministryProjects.project: Gas-to-power transition roadmap and Deir Ammar FSRU
ministryProjects.description: Minister Joe Saddi held a two-day workshop with IFC representatives on gas-fired power generation starting at Deir Ammar, covering legal, technical and financing aspects of a floating storage regasification unit and a new gas power plant, concluding with a roadmap.

ministryProjects.project: Sewage networks and treatment plants for Jurd Batroun villages
ministryProjects.description: Batroun highland mayors meeting in Tannourine asked the Minister of Energy and Water to declare the Jurd Batroun sewage project a national priority, prepare final studies, secure financing and include it in annual budgets and donor funding plans.

ministryProjects.project: UNDP Climate Promise support to Lebanon's climate action planning
ministryProjects.description: UNDP and the Ministry of Environment held a panel on Lebanon's climate progress; UNDP support to the Ministry falls within the Climate Promise initiative funded by bilateral donors including Belgium, Denmark, the EU, Germany, Iceland, Italy, Japan, Latvia and Luxembourg.

ministryProjects.project: Karantina Sorting Facility rehabilitation works (site visit)
funders: a multi-donor trust fund administered by the World Bank
ministryProjects.description: A site visit was conducted to the Karantina Sorting Facility under the UNDP-implemented Beirut Critical Environment Recovery, Restoration and Waste Management Programme financed by the LFF. Full rehabilitation was expected by end of June 2025.

ministryProjects.project: Beirut Critical Environment Recovery and Waste Management - Karantina Facility
funders: a multi-donor trust fund administered by the World Bank
ministryProjects.description: A field visit reviewed rehabilitation progress at the Karantina Sorting Facility under the Beirut Critical Environment Recovery, Restoration and Waste Management Programme, implemented by UNDP with the Ministry of Environment and Beirut Governorate and funded by the LFF.

ministryProjects.project: Step4Nature theatrical hike at Machaa Chnaniir Nature Reserve
funders: Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation through AICS
ministryProjects.description: UNDP, in partnership with the Ministry of Environment, the Embassy of Italy and AICS, organised a theatrical hike at Machaa Chnaniir Nature Reserve under the UNDP-Step4Nature Project funded by the Italian Ministry of Foreign Affairs through AICS.

ministryProjects.project: Community-based Wildfire Risk Management in Lebanon's Vulnerable Landscapes
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Environment and UNOPS signed an agreement under the wildfire risk management project, financed by a US$3.48 million GEF grant administered by the World Bank, covering equipment, vehicles, joint operations centers and forest restoration.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon's Third Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC 3.0) process
ministryProjects.description: UNDP, in partnership with the Ministry of Environment and with Green Climate Fund funding, launched the inception of Lebanon's NDC 3.0 during a national workshop to update the country's 2035 climate targets.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Climate Policy Package (NAP 2025-2035, NDC 3.0, LT-LEDS)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Environment launched its Climate Policy Package at the Grand Serail with UNDP support, bringing together the National Adaptation Plan (NAP 2025-2035), the updated NDC 3.0 and the Long-Term Low Emission Development Strategy.

ministryProjects.project: National air quality monitoring network - Beirut phase
partners: Institutions hosting air quality monitoring stations
ministryProjects.description: A memorandum of understanding was signed at the Ministry of Environment with institutions hosting air quality monitoring stations and low-cost sensors installed in Beirut, as part of establishing an air quality monitoring network; the minister cited limited funding for starting in Beirut.

ministryProjects.project: Infectious medical waste treatment centre at Karantina hospital
ministryProjects.description: Ministers of Public Health and Environment opened Lebanon's first infectious medical waste treatment centre in a public hospital at Beirut Governmental University Hospital - Karantina, at a cost of USD 2.7 million granted by the EU under the TaDWIR project, implemented by UNDP.

ministryProjects.project: Urgent environmental recovery intervention plan
ministryProjects.description: Environment Minister Tamara Elzein said World Bank assessment of the previous war put environmental sector losses above USD 500 million, while current estimates indicate Lebanon urgently needs USD 300 million to restore environmental balance.

ministryProjects.project: Birds of Lebanon Guidebook
partners: Association for Bird Conservation in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: UNDP, in partnership with the Ministry of Environment and with support from the Government of Norway, launched the Birds of Lebanon Guidebook documenting more than 400 bird species, developed jointly with ABCL.

ministryProjects.project: EUR 32 million programme for conflict-affected areas
ministryProjects.description: The Government of Lebanon, the EU, Denmark and France through AFD launched a EUR 32 million programme supporting conflict-affected areas in South Lebanon and the Bekaa, covering local authorities, businesses, agriculture and employment.

ministryProjects.project: METAC regional technical assistance programme (IMF)
partners: IMF Middle East Regional Technical Assistance Centre
ministryProjects.description: Finance Minister Yassine Jaber chaired, as head of the METAC steering committee, the centre's annual meeting in Rabat with IMF representatives, donors and member-state finance ministers, stressing capacity-building support for public institutions.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: Hungarian support for Catholic schools, medical care and Bekaa humanitarian programmes
ministryProjects.description: Szijjarto announced Hungary will allocate 200 million forints (about EUR half a million) this year to modernise education in Catholic schools, fund medical treatment and services for Christian families in Beirut, and finance humanitarian programmes in the Bekaa.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation and digitisation of the MFA Attestations Department
ministryProjects.description: Minister Rajji inaugurated the rehabilitated Attestations Department at the ministry, rebuilt with donor contributions and now running a fully digital system that completes a transaction in under a minute; donors attended the opening.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: Lebanon-Germany development cooperation negotiations 2025
partners: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
Ministry of State for Administrative Development
ministryProjects.sourceFeed: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: At intergovernmental development cooperation negotiations at the Grand Serail, Germany announced it would allocate a total of EUR 149.65 million for 2025 to long-term projects supporting reforms, recovery and the most vulnerable groups. Several Lebanese ministers attended.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: EU-Lebanon Partnership Conference, Brussels
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants published the final statement of the EU-Lebanon Partnership Conference held in Brussels. The available excerpt contains only site navigation, so no further detail is confirmed.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: Paris conference to support the Lebanese Army and Internal Security Forces
ministryProjects.description: Speaking in Geneva, Foreign Minister Rajji said Lebanon is counting on the Paris conference to support the military institution and the Internal Security Forces so legitimate forces can complete control over all Lebanese territory.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: Irish allocation for displaced people in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: Foreign Minister Rajji was notified of Ireland's allocation of EUR 3 million for displaced people in Lebanon. The body of the article covers a separate call with Finland's foreign minister conveying support.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: German humanitarian aid allocation for the Lebanese people
ministryProjects.description: In a call with Lebanese Foreign Minister Rajji, German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul announced the allocation of EUR 45 million in humanitarian assistance for the Lebanese people.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: Canadian humanitarian aid package for Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: Canadian Foreign Minister Anita Anand informed Lebanese Foreign Minister Youssef Rajji that Canada has allocated USD 40 million in humanitarian aid to Lebanon, to be delivered through international humanitarian organisations.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.project: US immediate humanitarian assistance to Lebanon under the framework agreement
ministryProjects.description: At the signing of the Lebanon-Israel framework agreement in Washington, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio announced USD 100 million in immediate humanitarian assistance for Lebanon, in coordination with the United Nations.

ministryProjects.project: National Industrial Strategy
ministryProjects.description: Industry Minister Joe Issa El-Khoury presented the National Industrial Strategy, a road map for reviving the industrial sector over the coming years, at the opening of the Lebanese Industry Fair 2025.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanese Industry Fair 2025
ministryProjects.description: President Joseph Aoun opened the Lebanese Industry Fair 2025, organised by the Ministry of Industry and the Association of Lebanese Industrialists at Seaside Arena in Beirut, with 190 exhibitors over 10,000 square metres across four days.

ministryProjects.project: 2Circular project and Green Industry Finance Forum
partners: European Bank for Reconstruction and Development
ministryProjects.description: Industry Minister Joe Issa El-Khoury patronised the Green Industry Finance Forum organised by UNIDO through its 2Circular project, in cooperation with the EBRD and funded by the European Union, promoting a transition to green and circular industry.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon-Japan industrial cooperation and Japanese-funded industrial projects
ministryProjects.description: Industry Minister Joe Issa El-Khoury discussed cooperation prospects with Japanese Ambassador Yokota Kenji and thanked the Japanese government for its support in Lebanon, including the financing of projects that benefited the industrial sector.

ministryProjects.project: Regulatory and administrative advisory cooperation agreement with PFC International
ministryProjects.description: Industry Minister Joe Issa El-Khoury signed a cooperation agreement with PFC International to provide regulatory and administrative consultancy to the ministry, aimed at maintaining export readiness and cutting energy costs, carbon footprint and waste.

ministryProjects.project: Tripartite partnership to combat disinformation and hate speech
ministryProjects.description: Under the leadership of the Ministry of Information, UNESCO signed a tripartite partnership agreement with the OIF to counter disinformation and hate speech, including a large-scale media campaign, fact-checking training for National News Agency journalists and equipment.

ministryProjects.project: #Heik_Mnkammel national media campaign on the draft media law
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Information and the UNESCO Regional Office in Beirut launched the national media campaign #Heik_Mnkammel to inform the public about Lebanon's new draft media law currently before the Parliamentary Administration and Justice Committee.

ministryProjects.project: "Fact Check Lebanon" Fact Checking Unit
ministryProjects.description: With UNESCO support, the Ministry of Information established a dedicated Fact Checking Unit named "Fact Check Lebanon", along with a digital page on the Ministry's website and targeted capacity-building trainings for the unit's team.

ministryProjects.project: "Together, We Stay Strong" national solidarity and anti-disinformation campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Information and UNDP, in partnership with Dawaer Foundation, launched a national campaign to promote solidarity, counter disinformation and divisive narratives, and strengthen constructive public discourse.

ministryProjects.project: "Share Responsibly: Be Part of the Truth, Not Misinformation" national media campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Information and UNESCO, in collaboration with Tele Liban and funded by UNIFIL, launched a nationwide media campaign of 10 short episodes to counter misinformation and promote responsible information sharing.

ministryProjects.project: Panel on the role of media in building trust and countering hate speech
ministryProjects.description: UNDP Lebanon, in partnership with the Ministry of Information and the Dawaer organisation, held a panel discussion at UN House in Beirut on the role of media in building trust and reducing divisions during conflict; the minister called for support for the new media draft law.

ministryProjects.project: ICRC training on international humanitarian law and protection of journalists
funders: International Committee of the Red Cross
partners: International Committee of the Red Cross
ministryProjects.description: The ICRC, in cooperation with the Ministry of Information and under Minister Paul Morcos's patronage, held a specialised training course for journalists on international humanitarian law and journalist protection, and launched a joint protection initiative.

ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation centre for boys in conflict with the law, Warwar
partners: UN Office on Drugs and Crime
ministryProjects.description: An EU-funded rehabilitation centre for boys in conflict with the law was inaugurated in Warwar, Beirut, providing a child-friendly environment for around 100 juveniles previously held in Roumieh prison's juvenile wing.

ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation Center for children/boys in conflict with the law
ministryProjects.description: A dedicated rehabilitation center for boys in conflict with the law was inaugurated in Warwar, Beirut, jointly launched by the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, the ISF, the EU Delegation and UNODC; refurbished under EU-funded projects implemented by MoIM with MoJ.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Electoral Reform Initiative 2026
ministryProjects.description: LADE, with EU funding, launched the Lebanon Electoral Reform Initiative 2026 to advance electoral reform priorities including strengthening the Supervisory Commission for Elections and establishing Mega Centers.

ministryProjects.project: EU support to Lebanon's electoral processes
ministryProjects.description: EU Ambassador Sandra De Waele said the EU has allocated EUR 22 million over the past 15 years to support Lebanon's electoral processes, including voter education, electoral reform and technical assistance to the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities.

ministryProjects.project: UK support to Lebanon's Internal Security Forces and border security
ministryProjects.description: The UK has allocated more than GBP 180 million since 2009 for internal and border security in Lebanon, including GBP 69 million for the Internal Security Forces.

ministryProjects.project: Turkish grant equipping courtrooms for remote electronic trials
ministryProjects.description: Justice Minister Marie-Claude Najm launched the completion of the remote electronic trials system at the Baabda Palace of Justice, with courtrooms equipped through an IT equipment grant from the Turkish agency TIKA to the Ministry of Justice.

ministryProjects.project: UNODC support to equip Beirut courtrooms for electronic hearings
partners: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
ministryProjects.description: The Justice Minister said courtrooms and courts in Beirut are currently being equipped with the assistance of the UN Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC), as part of expanding electronic hearings to more courts.

ministryProjects.project: Increased funding for the INL narcotics control and law enforcement programme
ministryProjects.description: Caretaker Justice Minister Marie Claude Najm discussed with US Ambassador Dorothy Shea increasing funding for the INL programme on narcotics control and law enforcement with the Justice and Interior Ministries, and Justice Ministry projects that could fall under it.

ministryProjects.project: TIKA grant of IT equipment for remote court hearings
ministryProjects.description: TIKA coordinator Orhan Aydin met Justice Minister Najm over a decided grant of IT equipment to the ministry to let criminal courts hold remote hearings and interrogate detainees by audiovisual means, easing prison overcrowding.

ministryProjects.project: UNODC in-kind grant of IT equipment for remote trials
funders: UN Office on Drugs and Crime
ministryProjects.description: UNODC provided the Ministry of Justice an in-kind grant of IT equipment to run remote trials in a number of courts; Decree No. 7585 of 16/3/2021 was issued accepting the grant.

ministryProjects.project: Launch of the new Ministry of Justice website / digital transformation
partners: Office of the Minister of State for Administrative Development
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Justice launched a new website with a modern design meeting international standards, offering services related to the judicial system and courts, as part of the digital transformation drive.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon-Russia agreement on the transfer of sentenced persons
partners: Ministry of Justice of the Russian Federation
ministryProjects.description: During Minister Ashraf Rifi's visit to Moscow, Lebanon and Russia signed an agreement on the transfer of sentenced persons; preparation of an extradition treaty was said to be in its final stages.

ministryProjects.project: New Douma courthouse building
partners: Our Lady of the Dormition Greek Orthodox Church waqf committee
ministryProjects.description: A new building for the Douma court was inaugurated on 12/08/2013 under Justice Minister Chakib Kortbawi; the move was enabled by Douma Municipality and a favourable lease from the Greek Orthodox church waqf that owns the building.

ministryProjects.project: Cooperation agreement on child protection in justice and health
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Justice signed a cooperation agreement on the child protection strategy in the justice and health fields with Hotel-Dieu de France University Hospital and the Saint Joseph University network, in the presence of Justice Minister Adel Nassar.

ministryProjects.project: Implementation of Lebanon's new pension scheme under Law No. 319
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Labour, the ILO Regional Director for Arab States and the NSSF Director General held a coordination meeting on implementing the new pension scheme under Law No. 319, with ILO providing technical support to government and social partners.

ministryProjects.project: New medical acts schedule and NSSF health and social benefits package
ministryProjects.description: Labour Minister Mohammad Haidar launched the new medical acts schedule together with a package of health and social measures approved by the National Social Security Fund, and said modernising the NSSF and its technical infrastructure is a priority.

ministryProjects.project: National tripartite dialogue on employment protection and enterprise recovery
