ministryProjects.description: The ILO held in Beirut the first national tripartite dialogue on employment protection, enterprise recovery and economic resilience, attended by Labour Minister Mohammad Haidar, government bodies, employers, workers, UN agencies and development partners.

ministryProjects.project: School grant (education allowance) for workers' children
ministryProjects.description: Labour Minister Mohammad Haidar said the ministry approved the school grant last week, with the decree due in the Official Gazette the following week so payment can begin; its value is about LBP 36 million per child within a set ceiling.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon-Egypt electronic data linkage agreement between labour ministries
ministryProjects.description: Labour Minister Mohammad Haidar and his Egyptian counterpart finalised a draft electronic linkage agreement between the two labour ministries and agreed to sign it in Beirut at a later date, to improve data exchange and labour market regulation.

ministryProjects.project: Tripartite MoU to coordinate international support for the Lebanese Army
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of National Defense, UNSCOL and UNDP signed a Tripartite Memorandum of Understanding to coordinate international support for the Lebanese Army, with financial support from the EU, Germany, France, Spain, Norway, Denmark and the Netherlands.

ministryProjects.project: EUR 12.5M project to support the Lebanese Armed Forces
ministryProjects.description: The EU announced a EUR 12.5 million project, implemented by UNDP, to help the Lebanese Armed Forces lead recovery in Southern Lebanon, including clearing rubble and unexploded ordnance and repairing water networks and public health centres.

ministryProjects.project: EU project supporting the Lebanese Armed Forces in recovery in Southern Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: The European Union announced a new EUR 12.5 million project, implemented by UNDP, to support the Lebanese Armed Forces in leading recovery in Southern Lebanon, including rubble and UXO clearance and repair of water networks and public health centres.

ministryProjects.project: Hungarian contribution via the EU to re-arming the Lebanese Army
partners: Ministry of Foreign Affairs and Emigrants
ministryProjects.description: Hungarian Foreign Minister Peter Szijjarto announced during his visit to the Lebanese Foreign Ministry that Hungary will contribute EUR 1.5 million through the European Union to fund the re-arming of the Lebanese Army.

ministryProjects.project: Saudi emergency grant to the Lebanese Army
ministryProjects.description: Justice Minister Rifi hailed Saudi Arabia's exceptional USD 1 billion aid to the Lebanese Army, recalling an earlier USD 100 million provided to the Army and Internal Security Forces and a USD 3 billion support programme.

ministryProjects.project: Saudi military grant to the Lebanese Army executed through France
ministryProjects.description: Rifi said the Saudi military grant to the Lebanese Army, worth USD 3 billion, will be implemented through the French state and is proceeding as planned, while the government's army development plan is estimated at USD 4.7 billion.

ministryProjects.project: US security assistance to the Lebanese Armed Forces and Internal Security Forces
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 237 million (including USD 192.7 million to the LAF and USD 45 million to the Internal Security Forces)
ministryProjects.description: The United States has provided more than USD 237 million in security assistance to Lebanon, including USD 192.7 million to the Lebanese Armed Forces and USD 45 million to the Internal Security Forces, with legislation linking continued aid to progress on disarmament.

ministryProjects.project: Support agreement for the Lebanon Mine Action Center (LMAC) 2026-2030
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of National Defense and UNDP signed a support agreement for the Lebanon Mine Action Center covering 2026-2030, in the presence of donors from the EU, Netherlands, Norway and Japan, to expand mine and UXO clearance, risk education and victim assistance.

ministryProjects.project: UK support to the Lebanese Armed Forces (training, equipping, capacity building)
ministryProjects.description: Following the Army Commander's visit to the UK, the British Embassy said the UK has allocated over GBP 120 million since 2009 to support the Lebanese Army through training, equipping and capacity-building programmes.

ministryProjects.project: US assistance to the Lebanese Army under the framework agreement
ministryProjects.description: Rubio stated the US War Department is ready to provide more than USD 30 million to the Lebanese Army, alongside creation of a trilateral military coordination group for Lebanon.

ministryProjects.project: Proposed US financial assistance to the Lebanese Army
ministryProjects.description: Senator Elissa Slotkin announced, after meeting President Joseph Aoun, that she had submitted a request for USD 350 million in financial assistance to the Lebanese Army to strengthen its readiness to carry out its missions.

ministryProjects.project: Health sector damage survey for reconstruction
ministryProjects.description: MoPH is conducting a full scientific survey of damage to the health sector (hospitals, PHC centres, clinics, pharmacies) with the World Bank, WHO and AUB; the report will be submitted to the government and donors ahead of reconstruction.

ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation of damaged sections of Tebnine and Marjeyoun public hospitals
funders: International Committee of the Red Cross
ministryProjects.description: Repair of the damaged sections of Tebnine Public Hospital and Marjeyoun Public Hospital has begun, financed by the International Committee of the Red Cross; funding is being sought for other heavily damaged hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: Financial contribution to Beit Lif Public Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The financial contribution earmarked for Beit Lif Public Hospital, as an approved branch of Tebnine Public Hospital, in the ministry's 2024 budget was transferred, amounting to about LBP 50 billion (about USD 558 thousand).

ministryProjects.project: Settlement of EDL electricity bills for ten public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: Financial contributions totalling LBP 135,654,973,899 (about USD 1.515 million), budgeted in the ministry's 2024 budget, were paid to ten public hospitals in the South and Nabatieh governorates to settle their Electricite du Liban bills.

ministryProjects.project: Enhancing environmental health capacity and awareness in PHC centres
ministryProjects.description: Under MoPH supervision, IOM with Seed Global Health launched a project to build environmental health capacity and awareness among staff in selected primary health care centres, running from 2 January to 30 April 2025.

ministryProjects.project: Environmental Health Capacity and Awareness Strengthening in PHC Facilities
ministryProjects.description: IOM, with Seed Global Health and in cooperation with the Ministry of Public Health, launched a project to build environmental health capacity of healthcare workers in selected primary healthcare centres, running January to April 2025.

ministryProjects.project: Distribution of donated medicines to displaced people
ministryProjects.description: MoPH published lists of medicines received as donations and distributed to primary health care centres serving displaced people during the war; chronic disease medicine kits were distributed under a WHO programme funded by the EU. Total: 3,099,283 boxes.

ministryProjects.project: Turkish Hospital in Saida - construction and operation
ministryProjects.description: The Turkish Hospital in Saida, built with Turkish state support exceeding USD 20 million, was partially opened under the ministry's emergency plan; remaining departments are to open in the coming phase.

ministryProjects.project: Donation of an ambulance to the Turkish Hospital in Saida
partners: Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism
ministryProjects.description: During his visit, the Turkish Ambassador announced the handover of an ambulance donated by the Turkish state in cooperation with TIKA and the Turkish Ministry of Culture and Tourism to equip the Turkish Hospital in Saida.

ministryProjects.project: Support to dialysis units in 20 public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: Minister Firass Abiad presented the implemented phases of a project equipping dialysis departments and opening new units in 20 public hospitals, financed by a World Bank loan of USD 2,178,000.

ministryProjects.project: Strengthening Lebanon COVID-19 Response Project (SLCRP)
ministryProjects.description: The Government of Lebanon received World Bank financing for the Strengthening Lebanon COVID-19 Response Project, implemented by MoPH; the ministry issued a request for expressions of interest for an external financial audit covering Jan 2024-Dec 2025.

ministryProjects.project: Psychological First Aid training of trainers with the National Mental Health Programme
ministryProjects.description: Project HOPE, in partnership with the National Mental Health Programme and WHO, facilitated Psychological First Aid trainings and certification using a training-of-trainers model for 25 frontline responders in Lebanon.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanese-French health cooperation: hospital twinning and central lab rehabilitation
ministryProjects.description: The Health Minister and the French Ambassador reviewed joint projects, including twinning of Lebanese public hospitals with French hospitals in oncology, cardiology, dialysis and maternal health, plus rehabilitation of the central laboratory with Institut Pasteur and WHO.

ministryProjects.project: SAQIRH primary health care project
ministryProjects.description: The SAQIRH project, supported by France through AFD and implemented by PUI, Amel and Medecins du Monde, has delivered over one million primary health care services in 16 health centres since 2020; discussed at a seminar attended by the Health Minister.

ministryProjects.project: EU support to the Lebanese health sector and ministry digitisation
ministryProjects.description: An EU delegation led by Ambassador Sandra De Waele met the Health Minister and confirmed continued EU support to the health sector, notably primary health care, medicines and immunisation programmes, plus technical support for digitising ministry systems.

ministryProjects.project: "Aqwa" programme for children wounded by the war
ministryProjects.description: Health Minister Rakan Nassereddine and UNICEF launched the "Aqwa" programme providing health care and protection services to about 1,500 children injured in the war, implemented with INARA and the Ghassan Abu Sitta Children's Fund.

ministryProjects.project: Delivery of Inter-Agency Reproductive Health kits to MoPH hospitals
ministryProjects.description: UNFPA delivered 34 Inter-Agency Reproductive Health kits to the Ministry of Public Health for distribution to hospitals, supporting safe births for an estimated 1,680 pregnant women.

ministryProjects.project: Investment case study on tobacco control in Lebanon
partners: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control Secretariat
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, WHO, the WHO FCTC Secretariat and UNDP released the economic investment case study on tobacco control in Lebanon, which found tobacco use costs Lebanon LBP 5.3 trillion (USD 140 million) a year, 1.9% of GDP.

ministryProjects.project: Equipping ten public hospitals with energy-efficient medical equipment
ministryProjects.description: A ceremony under the Minister of Public Health announced completion of a project funded by the Government of Japan and implemented by UNOPS that equipped ten public hospitals with medical equipment and energy-efficient installations.

ministryProjects.project: Resumption of the school medical screening programme in public schools
partners: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The Ministers of Education and Public Health, with the EU and UNICEF, announced the resumption of the school medical screening programme, EU-funded and implemented between January and April 2025, covering about 300,000 students in 1,050 public schools.

ministryProjects.project: Inauguration of the IRCAD Liban robotic surgery academy
ministryProjects.description: The IRCAD Liban academy for advanced robotic surgery research and training was inaugurated at Mashreq Hospital in Sin el Fil under the patronage of the President, represented by the Minister of Public Health, following a twinning agreement between the Army Command, Mashreq Hospital and IRCAD.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement and installation of five CT scan machines (128 slices)
ministryProjects.description: Under the World Bank-financed Strengthening Lebanon's COVID-19 Response Project, the Ministry invited bids for five 128-slice CT scanners for Rafic Hariri University Hospital, Halba, Nabih Berri University (Nabatieh), Tibneen and Baalbek public hospitals; bid security US$50,000.

ministryProjects.project: EIB Global-WHO initiative to strengthen public health in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: EIB Global and WHO signed a EUR 10 million grant to re-establish Lebanon's Central Public Health Laboratory and prioritise medication provision and healthcare support for over 50,000 people with chronic diseases.

ministryProjects.project: Assistance & Care for War-Wounded and Affected Children (ACWA) programme
ministryProjects.description: UNICEF and the Ministry of Public Health launched the Assistance & Care for War-Wounded and Affected Children (ACWA) programme to provide essential services to children impacted by the conflict.

ministryProjects.project: Reaya Pilot Project Evaluation - Lebanon Health Resilience Project
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 120 million (total Lebanon Health Resilience Project budget)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health invited expressions of interest from consulting firms to evaluate the Reaya pilot project across primary health care centres, financed under the seven-year World Bank-funded Lebanon Health Resilience Project with a total budget of US$120 million.

ministryProjects.project: Delivery of 40 tons of medical supplies and emergency medical kits
ministryProjects.description: The EU, through support to UNICEF, delivered 40 metric tons of essential medications and 15 emergency medical kits to the Ministry of Public Health, for distribution to 300 Primary Health Care Centres and Primary Satellite Units.

ministryProjects.project: Handover of 40 tonnes of essential medicines and emergency medical supplies
ministryProjects.description: The EU, through UNICEF, delivered 40 tonnes of essential medicines and emergency medical equipment to the Ministry of Public Health, to be distributed across 300 primary health care centres and units, including 15 emergency medical kits covering about 150,000 people for three months.

ministryProjects.project: Delivery of 40 tons of medical supplies to the Ministry of Public Health
ministryProjects.description: The EU, through support to UNICEF, delivered 40 metric tons of essential medications and 15 emergency medical kits to the Ministry of Public Health, for distribution to 300 Primary Health Care Centres and satellite units and to support some 150,000 people.

ministryProjects.project: WHO support to maternal health and primary health care services
ministryProjects.description: Marking World Health Day 2025 with the Ministry of Public Health, WHO reaffirmed support to maternal and newborn health; WHO secures chronic and acute medications for over 500 centres and dispensaries and has supported 12 public hospitals with equipment and training.

ministryProjects.project: Initial financial support to Rafic Hariri University Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health announced the Ministry had provided initial financial support to Rafic Hariri University Hospital to modernise essential equipment and secure laboratory supplies needed to sustain medical departments and patient testing.

ministryProjects.project: French-supported health projects: primary care, quality assurance, hospital twinning and central lab
ministryProjects.description: Meeting the French Health Minister in Geneva, Minister Nassereddine discussed joint projects implemented with French support, notably primary health care and quality assurance projects, twinning between Lebanese public and French hospitals, and technical support for the central laboratory.

ministryProjects.project: Environmental and Social Commitment Plan - Strengthening Lebanon's COVID-19 Response Project (P178587)
funders: International Bank for Reconstruction and Development
ministryProjects.description: The Government of Lebanon, through the Ministry of Public Health, is implementing the Strengthening Lebanon's COVID-19 Response Project (P178587) under a World Bank loan agreement, with an environmental and social commitment plan forming part of the agreement.

ministryProjects.project: Tender for specialised medical equipment for public hospitals (PICU, NICU, PET Scan, MRI)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health opened a public tender, financed by a World Bank loan, to purchase specialised medical equipment for paediatric and neonatal intensive care units, PET scan and MRI machines in a number of public hospitals across Lebanon.

ministryProjects.project: Aseel Early Intervention Centre partnership
ministryProjects.description: The Aseel early intervention centre of the Imam Sadr Foundations, which works with children with disabilities and their families, marked 14 years at its new premises under the patronage of the Minister of Public Health, in the context of its continuing partnership with the Ministry.

ministryProjects.project: Enhancing Pediatric Healthcare - Phase Two
ministryProjects.description: After completing phase one, the Minister of Public Health launched the second phase of the Enhancing Pediatric Healthcare project, implemented with La Chaine de l'Espoir and funded by the European Union, expanding to more public hospitals and primary health care centres.

ministryProjects.project: Distribution of 33 emergency trauma surgical instrument sets to public hospitals
funders: European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations
Government of the Republic of Korea
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with WHO, distributed 33 emergency trauma surgery kits comprising 330 complete surgical instrument sets to public hospitals to strengthen trauma and emergency care readiness.

ministryProjects.project: Emergency strengthening of public hospital systems, blood banks and central warehouse
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with WHO Lebanon and Japanese government funding, launched a three-part project worth about USD 1 million to extend the Logistic Management System to public hospitals, strengthen hospital blood banks and expand the Karantina central medical supplies warehouse.

ministryProjects.project: Pandemic Fund project: One Health approach for resilience and recovery
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health and WHO launched the Pandemic Fund project 'Using the One Health approach to strengthen resilience and recovery' at a workshop attended by the Ministers of Public Health and Agriculture, with coordination foreseen between the health, agriculture and environment ministries.

ministryProjects.project: Hospital centres of excellence for strokes and clots
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health announced the creation of hospital centres of excellence for clots and strokes in every region, backed by a national plan covering imaging, emergency care and surgery at the Ministry's expense and in cooperation with the French.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement of medical equipment for public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health invited bids under the World Bank-financed Strengthening Lebanon's COVID-19 Response Project for the procurement and installation of medical equipment to be distributed to public hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: Introduction of the HPV vaccine into the national immunization schedule
ministryProjects.description: Speaking at the Gavi summit in Brussels, the Minister of Public Health said Lebanon is working, through continued cooperation with Gavi, on plans to introduce the HPV vaccine into the national immunization schedule by 2026.

ministryProjects.project: Transition plan for self-financing the national immunization programme
ministryProjects.description: At the Gavi summit Lebanon received a Vaccination Champion certificate, and the Minister announced the Ministry intends to launch a two-year transitional plan to move the national expanded immunization programme toward self-financing, calling on Gavi to support it.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement and installation of 13 CT scan machines (64 slices)
ministryProjects.description: Bids were invited under the World Bank-financed Lebanon Health Resilience Project for the supply and installation of 13 CT scan (64 slices) machines for distribution to public hospitals; bid security set at USD 90,000.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement and installation of laboratory and sterilization equipment
ministryProjects.description: Under the World Bank-financed Strengthening Lebanon's COVID-19 Response Project, the Ministry of Public Health invited bids for laboratory and sterilization equipment to be distributed to public hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement and installation of radiology equipment for public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: Under the World Bank-financed Lebanon Health Resilience Project, the Ministry of Public Health invited bids for 29 digital routine X-ray units with UPS and 27 mobile digital X-ray units to be distributed to public hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement and installation of medical furniture for public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health invited bids under the World Bank-financed Lebanon Health Resilience Project for 121 ICU beds, 490 electric beds, 152 mobile stretchers and 138 electrical dialysis chairs for public hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: Karantina medical warehouse upgrade and Logistics Management System
ministryProjects.description: WHO, in partnership with the Ministry of Public Health and with EU support, upgraded the Karantina medical supplies warehouse, delivering ICT equipment (laptops, printers, desktops) to implement the Logistics Management System for real-time inventory tracking.

ministryProjects.project: Health system reform roadmap with international partners
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health met representatives of the EU delegation, World Bank, WHO and the 3RF secretariat to assess ongoing health system reforms and set a short- and medium-term implementation roadmap presented by a WHO adviser.

ministryProjects.project: Central Laboratory project coordination with the Lebanese University
ministryProjects.description: At the Lebanese University medical forum the Minister of Public Health affirmed coordination with the university on the central laboratory project, as part of the National Health Strategy 2030 launched with local and international partners.

ministryProjects.project: WHO-Lebanon Country Cooperation Strategy 2026-2029
ministryProjects.description: Minister Rakan Nassereddine and WHO Regional Director Hanan Balkhy signed the 2026-2029 cooperation strategy covering primary health care transformation, health governance and system reform, and emergency preparedness.

ministryProjects.project: Awareness campaign on smuggled and counterfeit medicines
ministryProjects.description: The Ministries of Public Health and Information launched a joint media awareness campaign warning citizens about smuggled and counterfeit medicines that escape Ministry of Public Health quality controls.

ministryProjects.project: National drowning prevention awareness campaign
partners: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health and the WHO office in Lebanon, with national partners, launched the National Drowning Prevention Awareness Campaign at the MARSATI marine sciences institute of the Ministry of Public Works and Transport in Batroun.

ministryProjects.project: Vaccination campaign for displaced and vulnerable children
ministryProjects.description: Between December 2024 and April 2025 a vaccination campaign led by the Lebanese Red Cross, in coordination with the IFRC and the Lebanese Ministry of Public Health, immunized 19,000 Lebanese, Syrian and Palestinian children. The campaign was funded by Gavi.

ministryProjects.project: Climate, Environment and Health Needs Assessment for PHC workforce
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with IOM, Seed Global Health and the University of Melbourne, launched the findings of the Climate, Environment and Health Needs Assessment for Lebanon's primary healthcare workforce at an event in Beirut on 29 July.

ministryProjects.project: Full coverage of paediatric kidney transplants
ministryProjects.description: The Minister visited a child who underwent a kidney transplant at Al Rassoul Al Aazam Hospital, the first performed at the Ministry of Public Health's expense following his decision to cover kidney transplants fully for patients under 18.

ministryProjects.project: National Strategy for Digital Transformation in the Health Sector 2025-2030
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health launched the National Strategy for Digital Transformation in the Health Sector 2025-2030 in partnership with UNICEF; the strategy was developed with UNICEF technical support and the Copenhagen Institute for Futures Studies.

ministryProjects.project: National health laboratory policy development with Fondation Merieux
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health and Fondation Merieux's president signed a two-year cooperation agreement to develop Lebanon's national health laboratory policy, providing technical support for diagnostics, capacity building and mapping of the existing laboratory system.

ministryProjects.project: Strengthening Lebanon COVID-19 Response Project: laboratory equipment for the Central Lab
ministryProjects.description: Under the World Bank-financed Strengthening Lebanon's COVID-19 Response Project (Loan No. IBRD-94280; GCFF TF No. TFB8782), the Ministry of Public Health as implementing agency invited bids for laboratory equipment for the Central Lab.

ministryProjects.project: CT scanner for Dahr el Bachek Governmental University Hospital
ministryProjects.description: Dahr el Bachek Governmental University Hospital inaugurated a new CT scanner provided through a grant from the Islamic Bank in cooperation with the Ministry of Public Health, restoring a service that had been interrupted for about three years.

ministryProjects.project: Cooperation agreement with AUB Medical Center to strengthen public hospitals
partners: American University of Beirut Medical Center
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health and the President of AUB signed a cooperation agreement to support public hospitals through specialised training, capacity building, joint research and new treatment departments; the first phase starts at the Turkish Hospital in Saida.

ministryProjects.project: Equipment batch and bed funding for Sibline Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.description: At Sibline Governmental Hospital the Minister announced an equipment batch including CT and MRI machines, cardiac catheterisation equipment, digital X-ray and mammography, ultrasound, endoscopy and lab equipment, plus USD 100,000 to equip 25 new beds.

ministryProjects.project: Aqwa programme for children injured and affected by the war
partners: American University of Beirut Medical Center
ministryProjects.description: The Minister visited war-injured children receiving specialised treatment at AUB Medical Center under the Aqwa programme, implemented by the Ministry of Public Health with UNICEF and the EU in partnership with INARA and the Ghassan Abu Sittah Children's Fund.

ministryProjects.project: ACWA programme for war-wounded and affected children
ministryProjects.description: Launched in March 2025, the Assistance and Care for War-Wounded and Affected Children (ACWA) programme is led by MoPH and UNICEF with INARA and GASCF, and has provided 426 of 1,400 eligible children with treatment, surgeries, prosthetics and psychosocial support.

ministryProjects.project: Central Laboratory completion tender
ministryProjects.description: Opening the 10th international conference of the medical laboratory owners syndicate, the Minister of Public Health said the Ministry has launched the tender to complete the Central Laboratory as a cornerstone guaranteeing quality of treatment.

ministryProjects.project: New project to support additional primary health care centres with the Qatar Red Crescent
ministryProjects.description: In Doha the Minister and the Secretary General of the Qatar Red Crescent agreed on a new project to support additional primary health care centres, and discussed steps toward signing a cooperation agreement between the Ministry and the Qatar Red Crescent.

ministryProjects.project: Equipment package for Abdullah Rassi Governmental Hospital in Halba
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 700,000 for the CT scanner and an additional contribution of about half a million dollars
ministryProjects.description: The Minister announced a new CT scanner worth USD 700,000 from the Ministry, an MRI via the Islamic Development Bank, a cardiac catheterisation unit supported by the Qatar Red Crescent, and about half a million dollars more for Halba Governmental Hospital.

ministryProjects.project: New governmental hospital in Sahle - Akroum
ministryProjects.description: The Minister announced that, in cooperation with the Council for Development and Reconstruction and the Kuwait Fund for Development, work will soon begin on a new governmental hospital in the Sahle - Akroum area of Akkar.

ministryProjects.project: Mhammara municipal medical centre
ministryProjects.description: The Minister opened the municipal medical centre in Mhammara, built under a partnership with Offenbach Municipality in Germany; German donors funded its medical equipment and the Norwegian Refugee Council, financed by the German development bank, completed the rehabilitation.

ministryProjects.project: Cooperation agreement with the Qatar Fund for Development
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health briefed President Aoun on the Doha mental health summit and said agreement was reached to begin executive steps toward a cooperation agreement with the Qatar Fund for Development to support the Lebanese health sector.

ministryProjects.project: Pharmaceutical sector reform roadmap and national medicines system support
ministryProjects.amountRaw: more than EUR 75 million contributed since 2015
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry held a workshop on pharmaceutical sector reforms with EU support and in cooperation with WHO to set a reform roadmap; the EU said it has contributed more than EUR 75 million since 2015 to strengthen the national medicines system.

ministryProjects.project: Health projects package for Hermel including MRI for Hermel Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.amountRaw: more than half a million dollars
ministryProjects.description: The Minister announced health projects in Hermel including raising hospital coverage ceilings by 20 percent, supplying Hermel Governmental Hospital with an MRI machine within two months, and a government contribution of more than half a million dollars to the public hospital.

ministryProjects.project: Dialysis centre at Minieh Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.description: A dialysis centre was inaugurated at Minieh Governmental Hospital under the patronage of former PM Najib Mikati and the Minister of Public Health, created through close cooperation between the Ministry and the Al-Azm wal Saadeh Social Association.

ministryProjects.project: Financial support for Minieh Governmental Hospital dialysis department
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 50,000 for dialysis water treatment and USD 100,000 additional hospital support
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health announced allocating USD 50,000 to treat the water of the dialysis department and a further USD 100,000 to support Minieh Governmental Hospital.

ministryProjects.project: Cooperation agreement with the Qatar Fund for Development to support public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health received a delegation from the Qatar Fund for Development; talks focused on projects to support public hospitals, notably Rafik Hariri University Hospital, and on concluding a cooperation agreement between the Ministry and the Fund.

ministryProjects.project: Imam Reda Health Care Centre in Ghazieh
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health sponsored the inauguration of the Imam Reda primary health care centre in Ghazieh, described as a pillar of the national primary care network.

ministryProjects.project: Medicines tender to supply primary health care centres
ministryProjects.description: The Minister announced the signing of a medicines tender worth USD 10 million to supply primary health care centres, with a 53 percent saving allowing coverage to be expanded to more centres.

ministryProjects.project: Cabinet allocation for primary health care centres
ministryProjects.description: The Minister said the Council of Ministers approved USD 20 million as a contribution to all health care centres in Lebanon distributed according to the number of beneficiaries, alongside a primary health care project secured in the 2026 budget.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Health Resilience Project: procurement and installation of medical furniture
ministryProjects.description: Under the World Bank-financed Lebanon Health Resilience Project (Loan No. 87710; GCFF TF No. TFA5424), the Ministry of Public Health as implementing agency invited bids for the procurement and installation of medical furniture for distribution to public hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: AFD strategic cooperation agreement for the health system in South Lebanon
partners: International Committee of the Red Cross
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health and AFD's Chief Executive signed a strategic cooperation agreement to strengthen health system resilience in affected areas of South Lebanon, focusing on the operational performance of Tebnine and Marjayoun governmental hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: Coverage of hip and pelvic fracture prostheses for the elderly
ministryProjects.description: From Zahle the Minister announced the start of coverage of prosthesis costs for hip and pelvic fractures in the elderly at the Ministry's expense, at 65 percent in private hospitals and 80 percent in public hospitals, plus expanded coverage of cardiac procedures.

ministryProjects.project: Free surgical mission at Baalbek Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.description: A Lebanese medical team from Detroit performed 20 free surgeries for patients at Baalbek Governmental Hospital under an initiative of the non-profit Arab American Association, with Stryker donating all the medical instruments needed.

ministryProjects.project: Equipment support package for Sir-Dinniyeh Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister announced that the Ministry of Public Health decided to support Sir-Dinniyeh Governmental Hospital with equipment worth one and a half million dollars, and that a kidney lithotripsy machine will be provided to the hospital early next year.

ministryProjects.project: Chemotherapy unit and dialysis department expansion at Sir-Dinniyeh Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister sponsored the inauguration of a chemotherapy department donated by Haj Khaled Marei Jamal and the rehabilitation and expansion of the dialysis department donated by Hajja Fatima Jamal, with treatment covered at the Ministry of Public Health's expense.

ministryProjects.project: Chronic disease medicines procurement programme
ministryProjects.description: The Minister announced the imminent reactivation of the chronic medicines programme after signing a tender worth close to USD 18 million for medicines for diabetes, blood pressure, heart disease and others, plus a new tender for equipment for primary health care centres.

ministryProjects.project: First early scoliosis screening programme in Lebanon
partners: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: Under the Minister's patronage, the first early scoliosis detection programme in Lebanon was launched with support from Fondation Diane and ALAM Suisse in partnership with Hotel Dieu de France; a joint health-education committee will screen pupils in all schools.

ministryProjects.project: National lung cancer awareness campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, in partnership with the National Committee for Cancer Control, launched a national lung cancer awareness campaign warning against all forms of smoking, as part of the National Cancer Plan.

ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation of the primary health care centre at Qana Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health and the Indian Ambassador signed a memorandum of understanding to rehabilitate and restore the primary health care centre at Qana Governmental Hospital, funded by India.

ministryProjects.project: Service improvement project at Karagheusian Primary Health Care Centre
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health inaugurated a project improving health care services at the Karagheusian primary health care centre in Bourj Hammoud, funded by Japan, equipping it with an advanced ultrasound diagnostic device and a water purification system.

ministryProjects.project: Medicines tender for primary health care centres
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry conducted and signed a tender last month for medicines for primary health care centres at a cost of about USD 18 million, so that medicines become covered at the Ministry's expense.

ministryProjects.project: Equipping public hospitals in West Bekaa and Rachaya
ministryProjects.description: On a field tour the Minister said Khirbet Qanafar Governmental Hospital will soon receive modern equipment including a CT scanner, and opened chemotherapy and neonatal units at Mashghara Governmental Hospital, with equipment financed by the Islamic Bank and World Bank.

ministryProjects.project: Japan Economic and Social Development Programme grant for the public health sector
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health and Japan's Ambassador signed the Exchange of Notes and Grant Agreement for Japan's Economic and Social Development Programme, providing JPY 425 million to strengthen diagnostic capacity at Baabda Governmental Hospital.

ministryProjects.project: Executive plan to equip 33 public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health announced a comprehensive executive plan to equip 33 public hospitals across Lebanese governorates with USD 95 million financed by the World Bank and the Islamic Bank, implemented jointly with the CDR.

ministryProjects.project: National plan to equip public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: Prime Minister Nawaf Salam patronised the launch at the Grand Serail of the plan to equip public hospitals, financed by the World Bank and the Islamic Development Bank, under the title "Public hospitals equipping plan: a strategy for reform and balanced health development".

ministryProjects.project: IsDB-financed equipping of hospitals across Lebanese regions (CDR-implemented)
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 25 million for medical equipment and about USD 5 million for works
ministryProjects.description: The CDR said its main current project for the Ministry of Health, financed by the Islamic Development Bank, equips hospitals across Lebanese regions with about USD 25 million of medical equipment and about USD 5 million of works, due mid next year.

ministryProjects.project: Funding secured for two central laboratories
ministryProjects.description: The Minister told health officials in Baalbek-Hermel that the ministry regained its voting right at the World Health Organization and secured funding for two central laboratories.

ministryProjects.project: Public hospitals support campaign: equipment, maintenance and financial contributions
ministryProjects.description: The Minister said the ministry launched a campaign to support public hospitals with equipment, maintenance and financial contributions, with about 40% completed in the first six months and investment exceeding USD 100 million to be completed in the first half of 2026.

ministryProjects.project: Updated MOPH APP with MediTrack medicine verification
ministryProjects.description: The Minister launched the updated MOPH APP, integrated with the MediTrack medicine tracking system, allowing citizens to verify medicine authenticity, locate the nearest health facility and access health information, as part of digitising the sector.

ministryProjects.project: MoU with AstraZeneca for early detection of lung cancer
ministryProjects.description: AstraZeneca announced it signed a memorandum of understanding with the Ministry of Public Health to launch a national initiative on prevention, public awareness, capacity building and evidence-based early detection of lung cancer, aligned with the National Cancer Plan 2023-2028.

ministryProjects.project: New CT scanner and internal medicine floor at Rafik Hariri University Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister inaugurated a new CT scanner and a new internal medicine floor for 27 patients at Rafik Hariri University Hospital, part of the ministry's roughly USD 100 million investment in 33 public hospitals backed by the World Bank and the Islamic Bank.

ministryProjects.project: Qatari-supported rehabilitation of Rafik Hariri University Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister said a project to rehabilitate Rafik Hariri University Hospital with Qatari support worth USD 15 million is under discussion, to be followed up with the Qatar Fund for Development and the Qatari ambassador in Lebanon.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement of chronic disease medicines for primary healthcare centres
ministryProjects.description: At the annual primary healthcare meeting the Minister said the state purchased chronic disease medicines worth USD 8.5 million for the centres, a saving of over 50% against a real market value of USD 18 million.

ministryProjects.project: National campaign on type 1 diabetes awareness and stigma
ministryProjects.description: At the ministry's annual primary healthcare meeting, a national campaign was launched to raise knowledge about type 1 diabetes and break stigma associated with the disease, alongside new service packages for primary care beneficiaries.

ministryProjects.project: Renovation of the first floor of Dr Emile Bitar Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister inaugurated the renovated floor of Dr Emile Bitar Hospital in Batroun. The hospital director said the first floor was improved with support from the Norwegian development organisation represented by NCA.

ministryProjects.project: Opening of St Veronica Medical Center in Zouk Mikael
partners: Basilian Chouerite Order convent of Our Lady of Annunciation
ministryProjects.description: The Minister inaugurated the "St Veronica Medical Center" at the Our Lady of Annunciation convent in Zouk Mikael, an integrated health complex with a laboratory, radiology, physiotherapy, dental and outpatient clinics.

ministryProjects.project: Public hospitals support project
ministryProjects.description: The Minister said the ministry launched a project under Lebanese government patronage to support public hospitals, financed by the World Bank and the Islamic Bank at USD 100 million, with departments already opened in Batroun and Beirut Governmental Hospital.

ministryProjects.project: National Immunization Programme
ministryProjects.description: The Primary Health Care department's National Immunization Programme vaccinates about 0.5 million children under five in each national campaign against polio and measles, with support from WHO and UNICEF.

ministryProjects.project: Health Response Strategy (HRS) for displaced Syrians and host communities
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health set out a Health Response Strategy to meet the essential health needs of displaced Syrians and host communities and to strengthen national institutions, calling on the international community to reorganise aid behind it.

ministryProjects.project: Health system strengthening project in cooperation with the World Bank
ministryProjects.description: Ministry of Public Health page titled 'Project to strengthen the health system in Lebanon in cooperation with the World Bank'; the scraped excerpt contains unrelated pharmaceutical industry content, so no project details are available.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanese hospital accreditation programme (new iteration)
ministryProjects.description: With AFD support, a cooperation agreement was signed in January 2022 between MoPH and the French Health Authority (HAS), with ESA as local counterpart, to revise and develop new Lebanese hospital accreditation standards in line with ISQua requirements.

ministryProjects.project: Infectious medical waste treatment centre at Karantina
ministryProjects.description: The Ministers of Public Health and Environment inaugurated Lebanon's first infectious medical waste treatment centre in a public hospital, at Beirut Governmental University Hospital, costing USD 2.7 million granted by the EU under the TaDWIR project and supervised by UNDP.

ministryProjects.project: Opening of Imam Hussein Health Centre in Burj al-Barajneh
ministryProjects.description: The Imam Hussein Health Centre in Burj al-Barajneh was inaugurated under the patronage and in the presence of the Minister of Public Health, at the invitation of the Islamic Charitable Association.

ministryProjects.project: First financial ceiling for primary healthcare centres
ministryProjects.description: The Minister said the ministry will allocate a financial ceiling for primary healthcare centres for the first time, amounting to USD 20 million and possibly rising to USD 25 million during budget discussions, distributed by number of beneficiaries and service packages.

ministryProjects.project: State budget allocation for hospitalisation coverage
ministryProjects.description: The Minister said the state allocated USD 270 million to the Ministry of Public Health for hospitalisation coverage, a quarter of the estimated USD 1 billion needed to fully cover the roughly 1.7 million Lebanese without any insurance.

ministryProjects.project: 100% hospital coverage for displaced people from front-line border villages
ministryProjects.description: The Ministers of Public Health and Social Affairs announced a mechanism giving displaced people from front-line border villages 100% hospitalisation coverage in public hospitals at the ministry's expense, using displacement lists held by the Ministry of Social Affairs.

ministryProjects.project: Psychosocial support clinics at the Barbara Nassar cancer centre
ministryProjects.description: During a visit to the Barbara Nassar centre for cancer patients in Achrafieh, the launch of the centre's clinics providing psychological and social support to adult patients and their families was announced.

ministryProjects.project: National cancer awareness and early-detection campaigns funded from the ministry budget
ministryProjects.amountRaw: More than USD 1 million per campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Minister announced a colon cancer campaign in March plus breast and prostate cancer campaigns during the year, with the ministry covering diagnosis and the full treatment pathway from its own budget; each campaign costs over USD 1 million.

ministryProjects.project: Ministry funding of cancer and chronic disease medicines
ministryProjects.description: During a visit to the Children's Cancer Center the Minister said spending on cancer medicines rose from USD 32 million in 2024 to USD 103 million in 2025 after treatment protocols were expanded, with 200,000 medicine packs provided in 2025 versus 64,000 in 2024.

ministryProjects.project: National early-detection awareness campaigns for colon, breast and prostate cancer
ministryProjects.description: At an awareness event in Chehim the Minister announced three national awareness campaigns this year: colon cancer early detection in March, followed by breast cancer and prostate cancer campaigns.

ministryProjects.project: Opening and expansion of medical departments at Dar Al-Hikma Hospital
ministryProjects.description: The Minister patronised the ceremony inaugurating and expanding medical departments at Dar Al-Hikma Hospital in Baalbek, noting hospitalisation spending rose from USD 38 million to over USD 150 million in 2025 and hospital financial ceilings rose about 30%.

ministryProjects.project: Public hospitals support and equipping project
ministryProjects.description: The Minister said a project under the patronage of the Lebanese government, financed by the World Bank and the Islamic Bank at USD 100 million, supports public hospitals, with departments being opened, including in Batroun and Beirut Governmental Hospital.

ministryProjects.project: Opening of Lebanon Medical Center in Hadath
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health inaugurated the "Lebanon Medical Center" in Hadath, a new hospital offering services including robotic surgery.

ministryProjects.project: National cancer prevention awareness campaign and review of National Cancer Plan 2023-2028
ministryProjects.description: For World Cancer Day the ministry held a conference to evaluate the National Cancer Control Plan 2023-2028 and launched a national cancer prevention awareness campaign, in partnership with the World Health Organization.

ministryProjects.project: Full hospital coverage for stroke (thrombectomy) procedures
ministryProjects.description: The Minister launched 100% ministry-funded hospital coverage of catheter-based clot removal surgery for stroke plus one night of intensive care, as the first step of a national stroke campaign, to be performed within 24 hours of the stroke.

ministryProjects.project: Rehabilitation of the National Central Public Health Laboratory
ministryProjects.description: The Minister laid the foundation stone for rehabilitating the National Central Public Health Laboratory at Rafik Hariri University Hospital, in partnership with WHO, funded by a EUR 10 million EIB grant under the Economic Resilience Initiative plus Norwegian Embassy support.

ministryProjects.project: "Public Health Leaders" certificate programme
ministryProjects.description: The American University of Cyprus, with the Public Health Consultants group, graduated the first cohort of the "Public Health Leaders" certificate programme under the patronage of the Ministers of Public Health and Social Affairs.

ministryProjects.project: WASH programme in primary healthcare facilities
ministryProjects.description: During a visit to Al-Zahraa health centre in Zokak el-Blat with the Korean ambassador and UNICEF, the Minister reviewed the WASH programme covering health, water, sanitation and hygiene, implemented by UNICEF with support from the Republic of Korea.

ministryProjects.project: CHANCE national project on innovation in paediatric oncology and palliative care
ministryProjects.description: The CHANCE association concluded its national project "Innovation and technology in children's pain, oncology, psychiatry and palliative care" under the patronage of the Minister of Public Health, which also trained psychologists.

ministryProjects.project: UNICEF emergency response: medical supplies and mobile primary healthcare units
ministryProjects.amountRaw: US$48 million (UNICEF Response and Preparedness Plan requirement)
ministryProjects.description: UNICEF is distributing essential medical supplies in public health facilities in coordination with the Ministry of Public Health and has expanded UNICEF-supported mobile Primary Healthcare Satellite Units to 37 to provide consultations, immunization and urgent health care.

ministryProjects.project: UNICEF emergency response for conflict-affected children
ministryProjects.amountRaw: US$48 million (UNICEF Response and Preparedness Plan requirement)
ministryProjects.description: UNICEF scaled up its emergency response, distributing essential medical supplies in public health facilities in coordination with the Ministry of Public Health and deploying mobile primary healthcare units; its plan requires US$48 million, only 16 percent funded.

ministryProjects.project: Donation of 15 ambulances from Iraq to public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: The Minister received 15 ambulances donated by the Republic of Iraq. They will serve public hospitals in targeted areas to evacuate displaced patients and assist the wounded, with a share allocated to the Lebanese Civil Defence.

ministryProjects.project: UNICEF and WHO emergency medical supplies shipment
ministryProjects.description: The Minister received a 35.8-tonne shipment of emergency medical supplies: 32.3 tonnes from UNICEF and 3.5 tonnes from WHO funded by the European Union, delivered via the UNICEF supply bridge to support hospitals, primary healthcare centres and mobile health units.

ministryProjects.project: Arab health ministers' emergency support for Lebanon's health sector
ministryProjects.description: The Executive Bureau of the Council of Arab Health Ministers held an emergency meeting and decided on urgent support for Lebanon's health sector. The Minister presented needs of USD 41 million, USD 51 million, USD 10 million and USD 5.25 million for various health priorities.

ministryProjects.project: Health coverage and medicine supply for displaced people in shelters
ministryProjects.description: During visits to two Beirut shelters the Minister said the ministry supplies chronic and acute medicines to shelters and linked primary healthcare centres, and has decided to fully cover hospitalisation for uninsured displaced patients in public and contracted private hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: Medical aid shipment via the European humanitarian air bridge
ministryProjects.description: The Minister received a 14.3-tonne shipment of medical, surgical and emergency supplies from UNFPA and WHO, funded by the European Union through the European air bridge, for distribution to hospitals, primary healthcare and emergency centres.

ministryProjects.project: First shipment of life-saving reproductive health supplies (UNFPA/EU airbridge)
ministryProjects.description: UNFPA received its first shipment of life-saving maternal and reproductive health medicines and supplies in Beirut, delivered in close coordination with the Ministry of Public Health and made possible through EU support via the EU airbridge.

ministryProjects.project: Shipment of trauma and emergency health supplies for Lebanon's health system
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with WHO and UNICEF, received 3.5 tons of trauma and emergency health supplies provided by WHO at Rafik Hariri International Airport, funded through ECHO, to sustain services in hospitals, PHC centres and mobile health units.

ministryProjects.project: National health emergency preparedness plan
ministryProjects.description: The Minister presented the ministry's national emergency plan to strengthen hospital and health workforce readiness, secure essential medicines, supplies and emergency equipment, and coordinate ambulance and shelter response during the aggression.

ministryProjects.project: WHO support to the national health emergency response
ministryProjects.description: WHO is delivering medical supplies, training health workers, supporting the Public Health Emergency Operations Centre and coordinating the health response, and will continue working closely with the Ministry of Public Health on access to essential health services.

ministryProjects.project: WHO Flash Appeal for urgent health needs - Lebanon allocation
ministryProjects.amountRaw: US$ 10 million (of a US$ 30 million regional appeal)
ministryProjects.description: On 2 April WHO launched a Flash Appeal for US$ 30 million over six months across the five most affected countries in the Region, including US$ 10 million for Lebanon, to be delivered working closely with the Ministry of Public Health.

ministryProjects.project: National Immunization Strategy
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health launched the National Immunization Strategy in cooperation with the European Union, UNICEF, the Lebanese Red Cross and Gavi at Rafik Hariri University Hospital, to sustain vaccination services and improve coverage for all children.

ministryProjects.project: French humanitarian air shipment of medicines to the health sector
ministryProjects.description: A French humanitarian aid plane carrying 28 tonnes of medicines and medical supplies arrived at Rafic Hariri International Airport and was handed to the Ministry of Health for distribution to hospitals and health centres. It is the third such French shipment.

ministryProjects.project: Medical protocol to protect runners and athletes
partners: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health agreed with the Beirut Marathon Association to develop a medical protocol protecting runners and athletes, with primary healthcare centres offering preventive medical tests at reduced prices.

ministryProjects.project: European Humanitarian Air Bridge to Lebanon (sixth rotation)
ministryProjects.description: Minister Nassereddine and EU Commissioner Hadja Lahbib visited the Karantina central medical warehouse, where he received first aid kits from the sixth European humanitarian air bridge; a further 41+ tonnes of life-saving supplies were due to arrive.

ministryProjects.project: EU assistance to Lebanon since 2011
ministryProjects.description: EU Commissioner Hadja Lahbib said Lebanon tops the EU's priorities and that since 2011 the European Union has provided more than EUR 3.5 billion, of which more than EUR 1 billion [excerpt truncated].

ministryProjects.project: Public digital dashboard on war casualties and distribution of medical aid
ministryProjects.description: Minister Nassereddine launched a public digital dashboard on the ministry website showing casualty figures, the response to displacement, and detailed figures on medical and pharmaceutical grants distributed across Lebanese regions.

ministryProjects.project: State support to the health sector since 3 March 2026
ministryProjects.description: The minister said that despite the financial crisis the state, through the Ministry of Public Health, provided USD 12,370,000 in support to the health sector, enabling public hospitals to keep operating.

ministryProjects.project: In-kind medical grants from Egypt, Jordan, Qatar, France and Greece
ministryProjects.description: In-kind grants received by the ministry were valued at about USD 3 million from Egypt, Jordan, Qatar, France and Greece, with continued support from the EU, WHO, UNICEF, UNFPA, ICRC, MSF Belgium and Switzerland and Qatar Red Crescent.

ministryProjects.project: POCUS project to strengthen emergency diagnostic capacity in public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: Minister Nassereddine launched a project to strengthen emergency diagnostic capacity using point-of-care ultrasound (POCUS) in Lebanon's public hospitals, with local and international partners, at Rafic Hariri University Hospital.

ministryProjects.project: Third CERF-funded reproductive health supply shipment via EU Humanitarian Air Bridge
ministryProjects.description: A third shipment of lifesaving reproductive health supplies arrived in Lebanon via the EU Humanitarian Air Bridge in coordination with the Ministry of Public Health and Ministry of Social Affairs. Funded by CERF, it includes 68 inter-agency kits for 12,500+ women and girls.

ministryProjects.project: UNFPA grant of medicines and medical supplies for public hospitals
ministryProjects.description: Minister Nassereddine received a UNFPA grant of 14 tonnes of medicines and medical supplies for public hospitals, ensuring maternal and reproductive health care for 13,500 displaced pregnant women, plus family planning and blood transfusion supplies.

ministryProjects.project: Health platform and treatment coverage for children injured by the war
partners: Ministry of Education and Higher Education
ministryProjects.description: The parliamentary Women and Child Committee recommended that the Ministry of Public Health cover treatment costs for children injured by the war until age 18 and register them on a dedicated platform the ministry is preparing to launch.

ministryProjects.project: Universal Health Coverage draft law
ministryProjects.description: MP Bilal Abdallah said the universal health coverage project, begun when Ghassan Hasbani headed the Health Ministry, was prepared to international standards in coordination with the World Bank and WHO and is now before the joint parliamentary committees.

ministryProjects.project: 100% health coverage in public hospitals for the displaced and war wounded
ministryProjects.description: Minister Nassereddine toured Nabatieh hospitals, including Nabih Berri Governmental University Hospital, to assess damage from the Israeli offensive and needs, affirming the ministry's initiative of 100% coverage in public hospitals for all displaced and wounded.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon-Iraq bilateral health cooperation and support to Lebanon's health sector
ministryProjects.description: Minister Nassereddine met his Iraqi counterpart in Baghdad on bilateral health cooperation and securing support for Lebanon's health sector, in exchange for Lebanese expertise in emergency management; he thanked Iraq for wartime support.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon-Iraq health sector cooperation and support
ministryProjects.description: Health Minister Rakan Nasreddine met his Iraqi counterpart in Baghdad on bilateral health cooperation and securing support for Lebanon's health sector, in exchange for Lebanese expertise in emergency management and health services for Iraq.

ministryProjects.project: Tobacco Control Investment Case Study in Lebanon
partners: WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control
ministryProjects.description: Under the patronage of the Minister of Public Health, the Ministry, WHO, the WHO FCTC and UNDP launched the Tobacco Control Investment Case Study, finding Lebanon could avert over $400 million in economic losses and save 40 000 lives in 15 years.

ministryProjects.project: WHO support to Lebanon's health emergency response
ministryProjects.amountRaw: US$ 37 million (additional health sector requirement in the Lebanon Flash Appeal, March-May 2026)
ministryProjects.description: WHO is delivering medical supplies, training health workers and supporting the Public Health Emergency Operations Center; a convoy of four trucks with trauma and surgery supplies arrived on 1 April 2026. Health partners require an additional US$ 37 million.

ministryProjects.project: Shipment of 3.5 tons of trauma and emergency health supplies
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with WHO and UNICEF, received at Rafik Hariri International Airport 3.5 tons of trauma and emergency health supplies provided by WHO through support from ECHO, to sustain services in hospitals, PHC centres and mobile health units.

ministryProjects.project: National Cancer Plan 2023-2028
ministryProjects.description: On World Cancer Day the Ministry of Public Health, with WHO and national stakeholders, highlighted progress under the National Cancer Plan 2023-2028 and the need to consolidate governance and invest in sustainable cancer control.

ministryProjects.project: Pharmaceutical sector reform roadmap national workshop
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with EU financial support and WHO collaboration, convened a national workshop on 17 October 2025 to shape a pharmaceutical reform roadmap. The EU has contributed over EUR 75 million since 2015 to the national medication system.

ministryProjects.project: EU-funded good manufacturing practices (GMP) and PIC/S preparation programme
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with WHO technical collaboration, is leading a major EU-funded programme to strengthen good manufacturing practices and prepare Lebanon for the Pharmaceutical Inspection Co-operation Scheme.

ministryProjects.project: 2025 national influenza vaccination campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with WHO and funded by PIVI which provided the vaccines, launched the 2025 national influenza vaccination campaign at Rafik Hariri University Hospital to protect vulnerable groups and institutionalize influenza vaccination.

ministryProjects.project: WHO-Lebanon Country Cooperation Strategy 2026-2030 launch
ministryProjects.description: During her visit the WHO Regional Director met the Minister of Public Health and Minister of Finance and participated in the launch of the WHO-Lebanon Country Cooperation Strategy, calling for increased domestic and international investment in health.

ministryProjects.project: WHO support to primary health care and public hospitals (World Health Day 2025)
ministryProjects.description: Marking World Health Day 2025 with the Ministry of Public Health, WHO reported securing chronic and acute medications for over 500 centres and dispensaries benefiting more than 250 000 people, and support to 12 public hospitals with equipment and training.

ministryProjects.project: Delivery of 116 metric tonnes of trauma, cholera and mental health supplies
funders: European Civil Protection and Humanitarian Aid Operations
partners: Government of the United Arab Emirates
ministryProjects.description: WHO delivered over 116 metric tonnes of trauma, surgical, cholera and mental health supplies valued at US$ 2 million to referral hospitals across Lebanon, donated by ECHO and flown in via flights facilitated by the UAE government.

ministryProjects.project: Preemptive oral cholera vaccination (OCV) campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health launched a preemptive oral cholera vaccination campaign targeting 350 000 people in high-risk areas across 5 governorates; 130 field teams had administered more than 133 000 doses.

ministryProjects.project: Seven PSA oxygen generation plants in public hospitals (Baabda plant launch)
funders: German government through KfW Development Bank
ministryProjects.description: Baabda Governmental University Hospital launched its oxygen generation plant, one of 7 set up by WHO Lebanon in public hospitals and funded by Germany via KfW, part of a EUR 40.5 million project with the Ministry of Public Health.

ministryProjects.project: Italian-funded oncology medications for the central drug warehouse
ministryProjects.description: Italy's contribution to procuring oncology medications through WHO's Bilateral Emergency Fund reached 1 250 000 euros over two years, benefiting over 300 children and 1000 adult patients supplied via the Ministry's central drug warehouse.

ministryProjects.project: MoU with Task Force for Global Health (PIVI) on influenza vaccine
partners: US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention
ministryProjects.description: A memorandum of understanding between the Task Force for Global Health and the Ministry of Public Health, overseen by WHO, establishes a 3-5 year partnership in which PIVI donates influenza vaccines and provides technical support.

ministryProjects.project: Arrival of an additional 900 000 oral cholera vaccine doses
partners: International Coordinating Group on vaccine provision
ministryProjects.description: An additional 900 000 cholera vaccine doses arrived for the response led with the Ministry of Public Health and partners; WHO stated it requires around US$ 11.2 million for the 6-month cholera response, of which only 29% had been received.

ministryProjects.project: Arrival of 600 000 oral cholera vaccine doses
funders: International Coordinating Group on vaccine provision
ministryProjects.description: WHO covered the full cost of 600 000 cholera vaccine doses from the ICG stockpile and provided technical guidance, working with the Ministry of Public Health; Sanofi-donated Shanchol vaccine is also used for prisoners and health workers.

ministryProjects.project: WHO-Italian Embassy agreement to strengthen hospital care
ministryProjects.description: WHO and the Italian Embassy signed an agreement to strengthen the public health system and hospital care in Lebanon, focusing on governance, infrastructure and quality of care, especially emergency care.

ministryProjects.project: Italian emergency donation of pediatric cancer medications
ministryProjects.description: The Government of Italy provided an emergency donation of pediatric cancer medications valued at 500 000 Euros, delivered to the Lebanese Ministry of Public Health through WHO.

ministryProjects.project: Delivery of 14 400 insulin pens to the Chronic Care Center
ministryProjects.description: With EU support through ECHO funding, WHO delivered a first batch of 14 400 insulin supplies (pens and needles) to the Chronic Care Center, serving over 2000 patients with type 1 diabetes.

ministryProjects.project: Handover of the reconstructed central drug warehouse
ministryProjects.description: WHO with UNICEF handed over the rebuilt central drug warehouse to the Ministry of Public Health, serving over 1 million beneficiaries via 830 primary health care centres; Australian Aid through UNICEF provided cold rooms and a photovoltaic system.

ministryProjects.project: IOM-WHO cooperation agreement supporting the national AIDS control programme
ministryProjects.description: IOM and WHO signed a cooperation agreement to continue supporting the national AIDS control programme, a joint programme of the Ministry of Public Health and WHO, made possible through the Global Fund's regional Middle East Response grant to IOM.

ministryProjects.project: Reconstruction of the Ministry's Central Drugs Warehouse
ministryProjects.description: WHO is overseeing the complete reconstruction of the Ministry of Public Health's Central Drugs Warehouse destroyed in the port blast, raising capacity from 3000 m3 to 8000 m3 at a cost of over US$ 2 million.

ministryProjects.project: Second phase of the national measles and polio vaccination campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Public Health launched the second phase of the measles and polio vaccination campaign, targeting 364 130 children in five governorates after the first phase reached 231 200 children.

ministryProjects.project: Launch of the Central Drug Warehouse reconstruction initiative
ministryProjects.description: WHO launched the initiative to rebuild the Ministry of Public Health's Central Drug Warehouse in Qarantina, doubling storage capacity to 2000 m2; UNICEF will provide 6 refrigeration rooms and a solar power system.

ministryProjects.project: Provision of essential NCD medications at 420 primary health care centres
ministryProjects.description: With financial support from the European Union, essential medications for noncommunicable diseases are available at 420 primary health care centres and dispensaries through the chronic medications programme operated for the Ministry of Public Health by the YMCA.

ministryProjects.project: National measles immunization campaign (Kuwait Fund donation)
funders: Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development
ministryProjects.description: The Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development donated US$ 4.6 million for the national measles campaign; the first phase targeted over 300 000 children in three governorates, with a second phase planned by the Ministry with WHO and UNICEF.

ministryProjects.project: National measles vaccination campaign in border villages
funders: Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health's national measles campaign, supported by WHO and UNICEF and funded by donations from the Kuwait Fund for Arab Economic Development, reached the border village of Tfeil, vaccinating children aged 6 months to 10 years free of charge.

ministryProjects.project: National measles immunization campaign launch (915 750 children)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, with WHO and UNICEF, announced a national immunization campaign targeting 915 750 children against measles, with a first phase in Akkar, North and Baalbeck-Hermel from 7 to 22 December and a second phase in early 2020.

ministryProjects.project: Health Policy Support Observatory
ministryProjects.description: The Policy Support Observatory was launched at the Ministry of Public Health under a tripartite agreement between the Ministry, WHO and the American University of Beirut to promote innovation, strengthen governance and provide evidence for health policy.

ministryProjects.project: Japanese support for chronic disease medications for children
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health welcomed Japanese funding, channelled through WHO, that will provide diabetes and thalassemia medications for 750 children via the chronic care centre supported by a special government fund.

ministryProjects.project: Mental health training for primary health care staff
ministryProjects.description: WHO supported the Ministry of Public Health in mental health training workshops funded by the European Union under the Neighbourhood Initiative, training 102 health care staff, plus 11 workshops on managing mental health emergencies in hospitals.

ministryProjects.project: NCD and mental health services at primary health care level
ministryProjects.description: A 2.4 million euro project implemented by WHO Lebanon will enhance access to noncommunicable disease and mental health services, supplying chronic medications to 440 primary health care centres in the Ministry of Public Health/YMCA programme.

ministryProjects.project: Medical equipment handover to Rashaya El Wadi Governmental Hospital
ministryProjects.description: Under the EU-funded project 'Conflict Reduction through Improving Healthcare Services for the Vulnerable Population in Lebanon', led by the Ministry of Public Health, Rashaya El Wadi Governmental Hospital received obstetric, neonatal, ICT and laboratory equipment.

ministryProjects.project: Emergency obstetrics care capacity-building for health professionals
partners: Lebanese Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology
ministryProjects.description: WHO and the Ministry of Public Health, with the Lebanese Society of Obstetrics and Gynecology and under the EU/IfS fund, implemented a capacity-building project on emergency obstetrics care, conducting ten workshops across Lebanon.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement of 7000 medical equipment items for 180 PHC centres
ministryProjects.description: WHO procured around 7000 pieces of medical equipment and clinic supplies for 180 primary health care centres, through the EU Instrument for Stability project led by the Ministry of Public Health and implemented by WHO with UNHCR.

ministryProjects.project: Provision of over 100 000 insulin vials to the Ministry
ministryProjects.description: WHO provided more than 100 000 insulin vials to the Lebanese Ministry of Public Health, serving around 500 insulin-dependent diabetic patients under the Ministry's essential medications programme, funded by the EU Instrument for Stability project.

ministryProjects.project: National polio immunization campaign
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health launched a two-round national polio immunization campaign for all children under five, with WHO and UNICEF; 1.2 million doses of polio vaccine were provided to the Ministry.

ministryProjects.project: Procurement of leishmaniasis medications and biopsy equipment
ministryProjects.description: WHO supported the Ministry with a strategic response plan, 12 treatment clinics, training and procurement of Glucantime medications and biopsy equipment, under the EU/IFS project funded by the EU and implemented with UNHCR.

ministryProjects.project: Mother and Child Health Care initiative
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health launched the 'Mother and Child Health Care' initiative at Rashayya Public Hospital under the EU-funded Instrument for Stability project, capacitating four primary health care centres for non-insured pregnant women and children.

ministryProjects.project: National hepatitis awareness campaign
ministryProjects.description: WHO supported the launch of a national hepatitis awareness campaign in line with the national hepatitis strategy; the government subsidizes hepatitis B and C treatment for poor people based on guidelines developed with WHO support in 2012.

ministryProjects.project: Provision of 13 vehicles to the Ministry of Public Health
ministryProjects.description: WHO Lebanon provided the Lebanese Ministry of Public Health with 13 vehicles with support from the Kuwaiti emergency fund, to support primary health care centres, the surveillance programme and communicable disease and tuberculosis control.

ministryProjects.project: National Polio Immunization Campaign (April 2014 round)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health launched a six-day national polio immunization campaign targeting at least 600,000 children under five, also covering measles, rubella and vitamin A. UNICEF provided 1.7 million polio doses and 1.3 million measles/rubella vaccines; WHO supported planning and trained nearly 4,200 vaccinators.

ministryProjects.project: Additional Polio National Immunization Days (NIDs) support
ministryProjects.description: WHO and UNICEF will support the Ministry of Public Health financially and technically to conduct two further polio NID rounds for all children under five. 1.5 million doses of trivalent OPV are under procurement through UNICEF, with WHO funding microplan implementation and logistics.

ministryProjects.project: Third National Polio Immunization Campaign (March 2014)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health, WHO and UNICEF announced a third nationwide six-day polio campaign starting 10 March to reach almost 600,000 children under five. UNICEF supplies 300,000 doses to private paediatricians plus 1.7 million doses to the Ministry; WHO provides logistical support.

ministryProjects.project: Expanded polio, measles, rubella and vitamin A campaign
ministryProjects.description: An expanded immunization campaign for polio, measles and rubella plus vitamin A supplementation is planned for April. WHO and UNICEF will mobilize their partner network to support the Ministry of Public Health in reaching almost one million children aged 9 months to 18 years.
