ministryProjects.project: Republic of Korea donation of essential medicines
ministryProjects.description: A handover ceremony at MoPH marked Korea's donation of essential medicines sourced from Korean pharmaceutical firms, coordinated by the Korean Embassy, KOICA and KCOC and delivered through three Korean NGOs under KOICA's RAPID programme.

ministryProjects.project: Donation of 14 ambulances and integrated medical supplies
partners: Office of Ayatollah Sistani's representative in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: Health Minister Rakan Nassereddine announced the ministry received 14 ambulances and integrated medical supplies from the Imam Hussein Holy Shrine in Iraq; its representative said further relief convoys would follow.

ministryProjects.project: Cooperation agreement with MECRA on clinical research and AI
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Health signed a cooperation agreement with MECRA to upgrade national clinical research infrastructure and strengthen health security using advanced digital technologies and AI solutions.

ministryProjects.project: Donation of 14 ambulances and medical supplies
ministryProjects.description: Health Minister Rakan Nassereddine announced the ministry received 14 ambulances and complete medical supplies donated by the Imam Hussein Holy Shrine in Iraq; its representative said further relief convoys would follow.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP)
ministryProjects.description: The World Bank Board approved US$250 million in financing for the Lebanon Emergency Assistance Project (LEAP) to repair damaged public infrastructure and lifeline services and manage rubble. LEAP is a US$1 billion scalable, government-led framework.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC), Beirut Naval Base
ministryProjects.description: Lebanon inaugurated its first Joint Rescue Coordination Centre at Beirut Naval Base, established with EU and French funding under the project 'Disaster Management, Port and Maritime Reform for Economic Recovery' with UNDP and IOM support.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Joint Rescue Coordination Centre (JRCC) at Beirut Naval Base
ministryProjects.description: Lebanon inaugurated its first Joint Rescue Coordination Centre at Beirut Naval Base, funded by the EU and France under the Disaster Management, Port and Maritime Reform project with UNDP and IOM support. The EU provided IT, secure communications and rescue equipment.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Port and Maritime Reform for Economic Recovery - maritime safety training
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Public Works and Transport celebrated the graduation of 392 LAF, ISF, General Security and Civil Defense personnel from a maritime safety and security training programme under the EU-funded project implemented by UNDP.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: First public intercity electric bus service connecting Jbeil and Beirut
ministryProjects.description: Lebanon launched its first public intercity electric bus service between Jbeil and Beirut, implemented by UNDP with GEF funding. Four electric buses with solar-powered charging at Jbeil Bus Station are expected to serve about 150,000 commuters annually.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Three feasibility studies for reviving land transport lines (North freight line, two Beirut-Beqaa lines)
ministryProjects.description: Press briefs report that a major service ministry is preparing to launch three economic feasibility studies to reactivate a land transport line halted since the civil war, limited to freight in the North, and to create two Beirut-Beqaa lines. The ministry is not named.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Cooperation protocol on railway and public transport engineering studies
ministryProjects.description: The Railways and Public Transport Authority signed a cooperation protocol with the Beirut and Tripoli engineers syndicates, under the patronage of Public Works Minister Fayez Rasamny, to provide technical, economic and strategic studies for transport projects.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Road rehabilitation and asphalting in Jbeil district
ministryProjects.description: MP Simon Abi Ramia met Minister Fayez Rasamny to follow up on delayed road rehabilitation and asphalting files in Jbeil, and announced a proposal for 'programme laws' with the ministry to secure financing for major development projects.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: Recovery plan for South Lebanon and West Beqaa: road opening, rubble removal and infrastructure
partners: municipalities and municipal unions of South
ministryProjects.description: Minister Fayez Rasamny told a municipal meeting that work has started on opening roads and removing rubble in safe villages, with infrastructure and paving next; he put the war cost at about USD 20 billion and said the state needs external aid for reconstruction.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of Public Works and Transport
ministryProjects.project: International air transport licences at Rene Moawad (Kleyate) Airport
ministryProjects.description: The Council of Ministers approved the Ministry of Public Works and Transport's request to grant regular international air transport licences at the Martyr President Rene Moawad Airport in Kleyate.

ministryProjects.project: ENABLE project - employment-intensive works in Bourj Hammoud
ministryProjects.description: A high-level delegation visited the ILO's EU-funded ENABLE project site in Bourj Hammoud, implemented alongside the Ministry of Social Affairs and local partners COOPI and AEP, observing Employment-Intensive Infrastructure Programme activities including town cleaning works.

ministryProjects.project: Emergency Social Safety Net (ESSN) cash transfers
ministryProjects.description: In 2024 WFP facilitated cash transfers for 794,000 vulnerable Lebanese under the Government's Emergency Social Safety Net (ESSN), as part of its support to 2.3 million people in Lebanon.

ministryProjects.project: Tensions Monitoring System Portal
ministryProjects.description: UNDP, in partnership with UNHCR, the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Ministry of Interior and Municipalities, launched the Tensions Monitoring System Portal, a digital platform making tensions data, analysis and conflict sensitivity tools accessible.

ministryProjects.project: Social Protection Academy - Foundational Course in Social Protection
partners: Universite Saint Joseph - Centre de Formation Professionnelle
ministryProjects.description: With EU support, the ILO, ITC-ILO and USJ-CFP held the Foundational Course in Social Protection in Beirut from 3 to 6 March 2025, training senior professionals from national institutions in line with Lebanon's National Social Protection Strategy.

ministryProjects.project: Road to Stability initiative - phase 2
ministryProjects.description: QRCS and Lebanon's Ministry of Social Affairs launched phase 2 of the QFFD-funded 'Road to Stability' initiative; 3,325 Lebanese families selected by the ministry will receive monthly cash aid for three months.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Response Plan (LRP) 2025
ministryProjects.description: The LRP Steering Committee endorsed the Lebanon Response Plan 2025, calling for USD 2.99 billion to support 3.6 million vulnerable people with humanitarian and stabilization support, and approved a one-year extension of the LRP for 2026.

ministryProjects.project: Horsh Beirut revitalization - first phase under ENABLE Programme
ministryProjects.description: The first revitalization phase of Horsh Beirut was inaugurated under the EU-funded ENABLE programme, implemented by the ILO with the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Municipality of Beirut. Works included a 1.7 km bicycle lane and rehabilitated sanitary facilities.

ministryProjects.project: Horsh Beirut revitalization under the ENABLE programme (phase 1)
ministryProjects.description: The first revitalization phase of Horsh Beirut was inaugurated under the EU-funded ENABLE programme implemented by the ILO with the Ministry of Social Affairs and the Municipality of Beirut; works included a 1.7 km bicycle lane, skatepark and sanitary facilities.

ministryProjects.project: National Disability Allowance (NDA) - domestic financing scale-up
ministryProjects.amountRaw: US$ 10 million allocated in 2025 (following USD 5 million in 2024)
ministryProjects.description: Lebanon began paying National Disability Allowance recipients directly from the national budget, with US$ 10 million allocated in 2025 and technical support from the ILO and UNICEF, reaching around 30,000 persons with disabilities at USD 40 per month.

ministryProjects.project: National Disability Allowance (NDA)
ministryProjects.description: A government-led programme providing direct income support to persons with disabilities holding a valid disability card, with EU and Dutch funding and technical support from UNICEF and ILO.

ministryProjects.project: Disability mainstreaming in the National Social Protection Strategy
ministryProjects.description: Led by the Ministry of Social Affairs with technical support from ILO and UNICEF and EU funding, to ensure persons with disabilities are included in shock-responsive and long-term social protection systems.

ministryProjects.project: ENABLE Programme - Career Preparedness Training Programme
ministryProjects.description: Led by the Ministry of Social Affairs under the EU-funded ENABLE programme and implemented by the ILO with the Lebanese NGO Arcenciel, the Career Preparedness Training Programme supports jobseekers with disabilities in digital literacy and career planning.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Response Plan (LRP) 2026
ministryProjects.description: The LRP Steering Committee, co-chaired by Deputy PM Tarek Mitri and the UN Resident Coordinator, endorsed the Lebanon Response Plan 2026, calling for USD 1.62 billion to support 1.5 million people in critical need, with a dedicated chapter on returns.

ministryProjects.project: Cash assistance for families affected by the aggression
ministryProjects.description: The Minister of Social Affairs said ministry teams visited more than 67,000 families affected by the aggression and provided cash assistance exceeding USD 20 million from donor funds over six months, building a database added to the ministry's social register.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Response Plan (LRP) 2026
ministryProjects.description: The LRP 2026 is the joint Government-United Nations response framework for crisis-affected populations in Lebanon; the 2026 cycle advances the transition to Government ownership, including cash assistance delivered through MoSA.

ministryProjects.project: Support to MoSA digital transformation plan
ministryProjects.description: WFP provided support to the Ministry of Social Affairs in advancing its digital transformation plan while assisting over 622,000 vulnerable people in January 2026.

ministryProjects.project: Government-led cash assistance and IDP self-registration system
ministryProjects.description: On 6 March MoSA launched the self-registration of internally displaced people to facilitate Government-led cash assistance; 500,000 people self-registered within 24 hours.

ministryProjects.project: Expansion of collective shelters for displaced people
ministryProjects.description: MoSA is preparing additional collective shelters with the support of humanitarian partners amid new and repeated forced displacement orders and a growing number of IDPs seeking safe shelter.

ministryProjects.project: Emergency cash support under the National Disability Allowance (NDA)
ministryProjects.description: MoSA, with UNICEF and the ILO, announced a one-off USD 100 cash support reaching about 6,000 families with children with disabilities from conflict-affected areas already enrolled in the National Disability Allowance, benefiting around 24,000 individuals.

ministryProjects.project: IOM emergency response appeal for displacement in Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: IOM appealed for USD 19 million to scale up its emergency response in Lebanon, where nearly one million people have been displaced. The appeal supports the response led by the Government of Lebanon, including the Ministry of Social Affairs.

ministryProjects.project: UN-Government of Lebanon Inter-Agency Flash Appeal
ministryProjects.description: A UN-Government of Lebanon Inter-Agency Flash Appeal seeking USD 308.3 million was launched to respond to mass displacement in Lebanon, aligned with the government-led response that includes the Ministry of Social Affairs.

ministryProjects.project: IOM Lebanon Flash Appeal - Crisis Response (March-May 2026)
ministryProjects.description: IOM appealed for USD 19 million to scale up emergency shelter, water, protection and health assistance for over one million displaced people. The appeal supports the response led by the Government of Lebanon, including the Ministry of Social Affairs.

ministryProjects.project: Flash Appeal: Lebanon, March - May 2026
ministryProjects.description: The prioritized Flash Appeal calls for US$ 308.3 million over three months to provide lifesaving assistance and protection to up to 1,000,000 people, including vulnerable Lebanese, displaced Syrians, Palestine refugees and migrants.

ministryProjects.project: 2026 Flash Appeal launched with the Government of Lebanon
ministryProjects.description: During a solidarity visit to Lebanon, UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres launched the 2026 Flash Appeal together with the Government of Lebanon, calling for increased international support.

ministryProjects.project: WFP emergency response to Tripoli building collapses and Akkar floods
ministryProjects.description: WFP delivered cash assistance to almost 500 affected households and food assistance to 230 displaced people after building collapses in Tripoli and floods in Akkar, in close coordination with the Ministry of Social Affairs.

ministryProjects.project: Italian support to UNHCR emergency response for displaced families
ministryProjects.description: Italy delivered an airlift of emergency relief items (hygiene kits, kitchen sets, blankets, jerry cans) for UNHCR in Lebanon and allocated EUR 10 million in response to the Lebanon Flash Appeal; distribution is coordinated with the Disaster Risk Management Unit.

ministryProjects.project: Lebanon Flash Appeal March-May 2026
ministryProjects.description: A Flash Appeal to mobilize $308.3 million for March-May 2026 was launched at the Serail in Beirut with the Government of Lebanon, UN agencies and partners, aiming to assist up to 1,000,000 people; it complements the LRP 2026 co-led with the Government.

ministryProjects.project: EU humanitarian airbridge delivering emergency relief items
ministryProjects.description: UNHCR, with the EU and the Governments of Ireland and Italy, welcomed a fifth EU-funded humanitarian airbridge flight carrying emergency relief items for displaced families, to be distributed through shelters and response centres.

ministryProjects.project: QFFD-funded emergency relief distribution for displaced families
ministryProjects.description: With QFFD funding, Qatar Red Crescent Society began distributing food and non-food items to 20,700 beneficiaries in Beirut, in cooperation with the Lebanese Red Cross and the Ministry of Social Affairs, including 4,140 food parcels and 3,741 hygiene kits.

ministryProjects.project: AMAN national cash assistance programme
ministryProjects.description: EU funding of EUR 40 million for the AMAN national cash assistance scheme, covering five months of payments for 90,000 of the most vulnerable Lebanese families out of 150,000 eligible.

ministryProjects.project: Institutional reform support to the Ministry of Social Affairs
ministryProjects.description: EUR 5 million of the EUR 45 million EU package will support institutional reforms within the Ministry of Social Affairs, including updating the beneficiary database. It is the first time EU funding is channelled directly through a Lebanese government institution.

ministryProjects.project: AMAN national cash assistance programme - EU direct support
ministryProjects.description: The EU announced EUR 40 million for the AMAN programme, Lebanon's national cash assistance scheme, covering five months of payments for 90,000 of the most vulnerable Lebanese families out of 150,000 currently eligible.

ministryProjects.project: Requested three-month extension of the 2026 Lebanon Flash Appeal
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Social Affairs formally requested an extension of the current Flash Appeal for an additional three months (June-August 2026). The appeal remained only 38 per cent funded, with approximately US$117 million received against US$308 million required.

ministryProjects.project: National Poverty Targeting Programme (NPTP)
ministryProjects.description: The National Poverty Targeting Programme, established in 2011 and implemented by the Ministry of Social Affairs, expanded after the 2019 economic collapse to deliver direct cash support at scale to poor and vulnerable Lebanese households.

ministryProjects.project: Government-led emergency multi-purpose cash assistance response
ministryProjects.description: More than 618,000 people received emergency multi-purpose cash assistance through Government-led response activities since March 2026, alongside 10.3 million hot and cold meals provided by humanitarian partners.

ministryProjects.project: Emergency Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (EMPCA) framework
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 20 per household member (capped at five members) plus USD 45 per household, monthly for up to three months
partners: Cash Working Group  EMPCA Task Team
ministryProjects.description: Interagency EMPCA guidelines establish a harmonized cash response for conflict-affected populations; Lebanese households are supported through the national Shock Responsive Social Safety Net and activation is led by the Government of Lebanon with the Cash Working Group.

ministryProjects.project: Revised 2026 Lebanon Flash Appeal
partners: Presidency of the Council of Ministers
ministryProjects.description: On 5 June the revised Flash Appeal was jointly launched by the UN Humanitarian Coordinator and the Minister of Social Affairs under the patronage of the Prime Minister, seeking an additional US$331.5 million for up to 1.4 million people through August 2026.

ministryProjects.project: AMAN social assistance programme
ministryProjects.description: Protesters in Tripoli criticised the Ministry of Social Affairs over the AMAN programme, asking about the fate of USD 250 million said to have reached the ministry for AMAN while beneficiary names were removed and payments halted for three months.

ministryProjects.project: Aman social safety net programme
ministryProjects.description: Social Affairs Minister Hanine Sayyed said Aman programme allocations rose from a few million dollars to about USD 55 million in the 2026 budget, benefiting some 160,000 families, with a request for USD 150 million in 2027 and health coverage coordination with MoPH.

ministryProjects.project: Purchase of prefabricated houses to shelter people affected by the aggression
ministryProjects.description: The Council of Ministers, chaired by PM Nawaf Salam, approved the purchase of prefabricated houses to shelter people affected by the Israeli aggression. The excerpt does not name the executing ministry.

ministryProjects.project: Social Safety Net Enhancement and Systems Building Project (World Bank loan)
ministryProjects.description: The parliamentary Public Health, Labour and Social Affairs Committee approved the draft law (Decree 3228) to conclude a USD 200 million loan agreement between the Lebanese Republic and the World Bank for the social safety net enhancement and systems building project.

ministryProjects.project: Citizen Budget of the Ministry of Social Affairs
partners: Basil Fuleihan Institute of Finance and Economics
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Social Affairs and the Basil Fuleihan Institute launched the first ministry-level 'Citizen Budget' in Lebanon, with support from UNICEF, to improve fiscal transparency and public access to spending information.

ministryProjects.project: AMAN social protection programme national financing
ministryProjects.description: The minister said the general budget contributes for the first time to financing the AMAN programme, marking a gradual shift of social protection from full external funding to state responsibility alongside continued donor partnerships.

ministryProjects.project: Humanitarian and development support for displaced and host communities in North Lebanon
partners: UN Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator office
ministryProjects.description: The acting North governor and UN humanitarian coordinator Imran Riza discussed the humanitarian and development response in the North, support to host municipalities, and expanding beyond relief to sustainable development projects creating jobs.

ministryProjects.project: National Economic Inclusion Strategy and partnership charter
ministryProjects.amountRaw: more than EUR 20 million (EU economic inclusion investment in Lebanon, 2023-2026)
ministryProjects.description: The Ministry of Social Affairs launched the Economic Inclusion Strategy with ILO technical support and EU funding, and a partnership charter was signed. The EU ambassador said the EU invested over EUR 20 million in economic inclusion in Lebanon between 2023 and 2026.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of State for Administrative Development
ministryProjects.project: World Bank loan for national digital transformation
partners: Ministry of State for Technology Affairs
ministryProjects.description: Minister of State for Administrative Development Fadi Makki said Lebanon is in the process of obtaining a USD 150 million World Bank loan dedicated to digital transformation, laying foundations for digital health and a wide range of government services.

ministryProjects.ministry: Ministry of State for Administrative Reform (OMSAR)
ministryProjects.project: Behavioral Innovation and Digital Transformation Lab (BIND-Leb)
ministryProjects.description: OMSAR inaugurated the Behavioral Innovation and Digital Transformation Lab (BIND-Leb) at its STARCO headquarters, funded by the EU and DANIDA with UNDP support, to help public institutions design and evaluate better services.

ministryProjects.project: Consultancy for the mobile networks Management and Operating Agreement tender
ministryProjects.description: The TRA published an RFP on the Public Procurement Authority platform for consulting services to prepare a competitive tender for the management and operation of Lebanon's two state-owned mobile networks (Alfa and touch); proposals due 30 March 2026.

ministryProjects.project: Electronic digitisation project for the tourism sector
ministryProjects.description: Tourism Minister Laura Lahoud said the ministry is working on an electronic digitisation project because it lacks accurate arrival figures, aiming to help the tourism sector attract investment and create jobs.

ministryProjects.project: Revised Flash Appeal for Lebanon, March-August 2026
ministryProjects.amountRaw: USD 331.5 million additional; USD 639.9 million total revised requirement
ministryProjects.description: The revised Flash Appeal continues the Government-led emergency response; partners seek an additional USD 331.5 million for June-August 2026 to assist 1.4 million people, bringing total requirements to USD 639.9 million, of which USD 185.9 million was received as of 31 May.
